tagline: The lake, the ravines, and a free museum night most weeks
heroDescription: Toronto's best days out are often its cheapest: a ferry to the Islands, a walk through the ravines, a market in Kensington, a free night at a major museum. Listings here come from the City of Toronto's open data and from local curators, and events update from the City's festivals feed.
contributors: City of Toronto (Open Government Licence - Toronto)

places.name: High Park
places.description: Toronto's biggest park: forest trails, Grenadier Pond, a free zoo, and cherry blossoms every spring.

places.name: Toronto Island Park
places.costNote: Ferry is $9.57 round trip for adults. The park itself is free.
places.description: A short ferry ride to beaches, car-free paths, and the best skyline view in the city.

places.name: Evergreen Brick Works
places.costNote: Free to visit. Some workshops are paid.
places.description: A former brickyard turned ravine park, with trails, ponds, and a weekend farmers' market.

places.name: Scarborough Bluffs at Bluffer's Park
places.description: White cliffs over Lake Ontario, with a sandy Blue Flag beach and picnic spots at the base.

places.name: Woodbine Beach and the Boardwalk
places.description: A long sandy beach and boardwalk in the east end, busy all summer and lovely on a winter walk.

places.name: Tommy Thompson Park
places.description: A wild peninsula built from construction rubble, now one of the best spots in the city for birds and bike rides.

places.name: Rouge National Urban Park
places.description: Canada's first national urban park, with marshes, forest trails, and no entry fee.

places.name: West Toronto Railpath
places.description: A car-free path along the rail corridor through the west end, lined with murals and gardens.

places.name: The Bentway
places.description: Public space under the Gardiner Expressway with art, events, and a winter skating trail.
places.seasonNote: Skate trail in winter. Check the website for dates.

places.name: Nathan Phillips Square Rink
places.costNote: Free to skate. Rentals cost extra.
places.description: Skate free under the arches in front of City Hall, usually from late November.

places.name: Riverdale Farm
places.description: A working farm in Cabbagetown with cows, pigs, and goats, free for everyone.

places.name: Allan Gardens Conservatory
places.description: A warm Victorian glasshouse full of palms and cactus, free to walk through on the coldest day of the year.

places.name: Toronto Music Garden
places.description: A waterfront garden designed around a Bach cello suite, with free concerts in summer.

places.name: Toronto Reference Library
places.hours: Mon to Fri 9am to 8:30pm; Sat 9am to 5pm; Sun 1:30pm to 5pm
places.description: Five floors around a soaring atrium, with free wifi, quiet desks, and exhibits.

places.name: Museum + Arts Pass at the library
places.costNote: Free with a Toronto Public Library card.
places.description: Borrow free family passes to the ROM, AGO, zoo, and more with your library card.

places.name: Fair Pass Transit Discount
places.description: Discounted TTC fares for Torontonians on low incomes.

places.name: Free Tax Clinics
places.description: Volunteers file simple tax returns for free if you have a modest income.

places.name: Credit Canada
places.costNote: Free counselling. Debt programs may have fees.
places.description: Free, confidential help with debt and budgeting from a non-profit credit counsellor.

places.name: WoodGreen Community Services
places.description: Job help, newcomer services, and free programs across east Toronto.

places.name: 211 Toronto
places.hours: Open 24 hours
places.description: Call or text 211 to find any community service in the city, in over 150 languages.

places.name: The 519
places.description: A Church-Wellesley community centre with free programs and drop-ins for 2SLGBTQ+ people.

places.name: Scadding Court Community Centre
places.costNote: Many programs are free. Some have a fee.
places.description: A downtown community centre with a pool, programs, and a shipping-container market.

places.name: Access Alliance
places.description: Free health care and settlement help for newcomers and refugees.

places.name: Toronto Event Generator
places.description: A weekly email of hands-on events around the city where you can actually meet people.

places.name: Snakes & Lattes Annex
places.costNote: Game fee per person, plus food and drinks.
places.description: A board game cafe with thousands of games and staff who will teach you the rules.

places.name: Gerstein Crisis Centre
places.hours: Open 24 hours
places.description: A 24-hour mental health crisis line for adults in Toronto.

places.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
places.hours: Open 24 hours
places.description: Call or text 988 any time to reach a trained responder.

places.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
places.costNote: Free first Wednesday nights. Check the website for prices and youth passes.
places.description: One of North America's great art museums, with a free night on the first Wednesday of the month.

places.name: Royal Ontario Museum
places.costNote: Check the website for prices and the free main floor.
places.description: Dinosaurs, world cultures, and natural history under the Crystal.

places.name: Gardiner Museum
places.hours: Mon to Fri 10am to 6pm; Sat to Sun 10am to 5pm
places.description: A small, lovely museum of ceramics, free on Wednesday evenings.

places.name: Aga Khan Museum
places.hours: Tue 10am to 5:30pm; Wed 10am to 8pm; Thu to Sun 10am to 5:30pm; closed Mon
places.description: Islamic art and culture in a striking building with reflecting pools outside.

places.name: Bata Shoe Museum
places.hours: Mon to Sat 10am to 5pm; Sun 12pm to 5pm
places.description: Thousands of years of footwear, and much more fun than it sounds. Free on Sundays.

places.name: MOCA Toronto
places.costNote: Free on the first Sunday of the month.
places.description: Contemporary art in a converted factory, free on the first Sunday of each month.

places.name: Graffiti Alley
places.description: Three blocks of murals behind Queen Street West, always open and always changing.

places.name: Kensington Market
places.costNote: Free to wander. Cheap eats everywhere.
places.description: Toronto's most colourful few blocks: cheap eats, vintage shops, and cheese mongers in old Victorian houses.

places.name: St. Lawrence Market
places.description: A huge historic food hall downtown, known for peameal bacon sandwiches.

places.name: The Stop Community Food Centre
places.description: Free community meals, a food bank, and cooking programs in the west end.

places.name: Daily Bread Food Bank
places.description: Find your nearest food bank across the city with no paperwork fuss.

places.name: Moonbean Coffee
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: A long-running Kensington Market coffee shop that roasts its own beans, with a small back patio.

places.name: Dark Horse Espresso, Spadina
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: A big, bright Toronto coffee shop on Spadina with long tables, good for a slow morning.

places.name: Pilot Coffee Roasters
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: The cafe at a well-known Toronto roaster's East York roastery.

places.name: Rooster Coffee House
places.description: A neighbourhood coffee shop across from Riverdale Park, with the skyline a short walk away.

places.name: Balzac's Coffee, Distillery District
places.description: Coffee in a two-storey Victorian pump house in the Distillery District.

places.name: Jimmy's Coffee, Kensington
places.description: A relaxed Kensington cafe with a patio that is hard to leave.

places.name: Type Books
places.description: An independent bookstore across from Trinity Bellwoods.

places.name: Courage My Love
places.description: A Kensington institution for vintage clothes, beads, and buttons at fair prices.

places.name: Double Take Thrift Store
places.description: A low-priced thrift store run by Yonge Street Mission, with proceeds going to its programs.

places.name: Value Village, Bloor
places.description: A big, reliable thrift store near Ossington station.

places.name: Free Concerts at the Opera House
places.description: Free noon-hour concerts in the glass lobby of the Four Seasons Centre, usually on weekdays.
places.hours: Mon-Fri noon-1pm
places.seasonNote: Runs fall to spring. Check the schedule.

places.name: The Rex Hotel Jazz & Blues Bar
places.costNote: Many sets are free or a small cover.
places.description: Toronto's long-running jazz bar, with live sets most days of the week.

places.name: Al Green Theatre (at the Miles Nadal Jewish Community Centre)
places.description: The Al Green Theatre is used for social and corporate event, theatre, film, concerts, dance; and lectures.

places.name: Alexander Muir Memorial Gardens
places.description: Named after the famous composer Alexander Muir. The gardens act as a path into the tranquil ravine system that includes walking trails. The gardens are open year round.

places.name: Alumnae Theatre
places.description: The theatre company is housed inside an old firehall and is the oldest theatre society in Toronto. Each year the company offers three productions.

places.name: Art Museum at the University of Toronto
places.description: Originally opened in 1996. The Arts centre puts a special focus on study collections.

places.name: Artscape Wychwood Barns
places.description: A heritage building converted into a community centre that hosts many events, festivals, farmers market and a children's theatre.

places.name: Ashbridges Bay Park
places.description: Ashbridges Bay waterfront park features large beaches, fishing areas, a marina, and the Woodbine Beach boardwalk.

places.name: Balmy Beach Park
places.description: Created in 1903, the historic park features a lawn bowling club, a playground and outdoor fitness equipment.

places.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
places.description: This unique-to-Canada architectural monument is made with 24,000 pieces of marble and stone. Discover the more than 10,000-year-old heritage of India.

places.name: Betty Oliphant Theatre (at Canada's National Ballet School)
places.description: Designed by Jack Diamond, the Betty Oliphant Theatre is used by the Canada National Ballet School as a training and performance venue.

places.name: Buddies in Bad Times Theatre
places.description: Buddies in Bad Times theatre is the biggest, and the longest-running queer theatre in the world.

places.name: CAA Ed Mirvish Theatre
places.description: A part of the Toronto theatre scene since 1920, the Ed Mirvish Theatre is a picturesque theatre to view special presentations ranging from concerts, comedy, plays, and many more.

places.name: CAA Theatre (formerly Panasonic Theatre)
places.description: Owned by Mirvish Productions, the CAA Theatre is the home of many famous theatrical productions.

places.name: Campbell House
places.description: The Campbell house dates back to 1822 and was once home to Judge William Campbell. It is the last example of Palladian architecture in Toronto.

places.name: Canada's Walk of Fame
places.description: Canada's Walk of Fame celebrates Canadians who have excelled in their respective fields for at least 10 years. The stars are displayed throughout the Entertainment District along King Street West and Simcoe Street.

places.name: Canadian Museum of Cultural Heritage of Indo-Canadian
places.description: The Canadian Museum of Cultural Heritage of Indo-Canadians is a museum committed to the understanding of India's rich cultural heritage. See BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir.

places.name: Canadian Sculpture Centre
places.description: The Canadian Scultpture Centre is headquarters to the Sculptors Society of Canada. The society showcases and exibits contemporary Canadian scultpures.

places.name: Canadian Stage (Berkeley Street Theatre)
places.description: Home to the Canadian Stage Company, the Berkeley Street Theatre presents an array of Canadian and international performances.

places.name: Casa Loma
places.description: Canadas foremost castle is complete with decorated suites, secret passages, an 800-foot tunnel, towers, stables, and beautiful 5-acre estate gardens.

places.name: Cedar Ridge Creative Centre
places.hours: Mon 9am to 8pm; Tue 9am to 8pm; Wed 9am to 8pm; Thu 9am to 4pm; Fri 9am to 4pm; Sat 9am to 4pm; Sun 9am to 4pm
places.description: Situated in a restored mansion, the centre features the Cedar Ridge gallery and rich gardens. The gallery highlights work from artists throughout the Greater Toronto area.

places.name: Centennial Park
places.description: Centennial Park is situated in Etobicoke and was opened in 1967 to celebrate Canada's 100th birthday. The park features sports fields, a conservatory, a ski hill, an Olympic size swimming pool, picnic areas and a Frisbee golf course.

places.name: Centennial Park Conservatory
places.description: The Centennial Park conservatory is located within Centennial Park. At a size of 12,000 square feet it features an arid house, a show house and a tropical house. The conservatory is open year round and is free to the public.

places.name: Centreville Amusement Park
places.costNote: Free to enter. Pay for rides.
places.description: Centreville is a 14-acre, turn-of-the-century, Ontario village theme park for children located on Centre Island, featuring over 30 rides.

places.name: Cherry Beach/ Clarke Beach Park
places.description: Cherry Beach is located within the port lands and features a dog's off leash area, the Martin Goodman Trail and a picnic site.

places.name: Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto
places.description: The building houses the P.C. Ho theatre, studios, conference rooms, a resource centre, a reception hall and an art gallery.

places.name: CN Tower
places.description: The CN Tower is an engineering marvel and one of the city's most visited sites. It features the world's highest wine cellar, a fine dining revolving restaurant (360), a glass floor. For the true adventure seeker, the Edge walk.

places.name: Colborne Lodge
places.hours: Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: This quaint cottage located within High Park was home to John and Jemma Howard. In 1873 the couple deeded the part to lodge to the City of Toronto. The house is a great example of a regency style building.

places.name: Dancemakers Centre for Creation
places.description: One of Toronto's professional contemporary dance companies, Dancemakers and the Centre for Creation is focused on the delivery of refined and passionate dance to its admirers.

places.name: Downsview Park
places.description: The vast green space allows for an array of small-to-large scale events such as culture, dining, leisure, sports, and recreation.

places.name: Elgin and Winter Garden Theatre Centre
places.description: The Elgin and Winter Garden Theatre features two completely separate theatres and is the last running double-decker theatre in the world .

places.name: Factory Theatre
places.description: The Factory Theatre operates two theatres in a Victorian mansion, where they have produced more than 150 Canadian plays, and various workshops.

places.name: Famous People Players
places.description: Located in Toronto's West End, Famous PEOPLE Players allows visitors to immerse themselves in a unique dining experience while enjoying theatre in the dark.

places.name: Fort York National Historic Site
places.hours: Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: Birthplace of Toronto in 1793 and scene of the Battle of York in 1813, Fort York has Canadas largest collection of original War of 1812 buildings. Open year round for tours, exhibits, and demonstrations.

places.name: Four Seasons Centre for the Performing Arts
places.description: The Four Seasons Centre for the Performing Arts is home to the Canadian Opera Company and the National Ballet of Canada.

places.name: Franklin Children's Garden
places.description: The garden, inspired by Franklin the Turtle, is an area to discover nature, play, while learning something new.

places.name: George Ignatieff Theatre
places.description: In the Trinity College community, the George Ignatieff Theatre acts as a creative hub ranging from events like theatre, conferences, and much more.

places.name: Gibraltar Point Beach
places.description: Surrounded by eastern cottonwood trees, the Gibraltar Point Beach is located on the southwest shore of Toronto Island Park. The Gibraltar Point Centre for the Arts is walking distance from the beach.

places.name: Gibson House Museum
places.hours: Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: Operated by the City of Toronto, the Gibson House is a museum where visitors experience an exquisite farmhouse and learn more about the rural development of the area.

places.name: Glenn Gould Studio
places.description: Located on the main floor of the Canadian Broadcasting Centre, the Glenn Gould Studio is a much-celebrated venue for its state of the art recording facilities and acoustics.

places.name: Gooderham Flatiron Building
places.description: Gooderham Building is a historic office building known for its unique location and triangular architecture.

places.name: Guild Park and Gardens
places.description: A sculptural alluring park and garden, the Guild Park and Gardens is rich in local history and a must-see for locals and visitors alike.

places.name: Hanlan's Point Beach
places.description: Situated on the west shore of Toronto Island Park, this beach is Toronto's only clothing optional beach.

places.name: Harbour Square Park
places.description: Located next to the Toronto Ferry Docks, Harbour Square Park offers downtown folks a spot to sit and watch the ferries travel back and forth to the island.

places.name: Harbourfront Centre
places.description: Popular 10-acre lakeside cultural site offers an eclectic blend of year-round arts, culture and recreation such as concerts, skating, music festivals and dance.

places.name: Hart House Theatre
places.description: A point of interest in the University of Toronto community, the Hart House Theatre and it's students produce an array of drama, dance, film, and music.

places.name: Historic Zion Schoolhouse
places.description: Built in 1869, the Historic Zion Schoolhouse has been restored to emulate schooling as it once was in the farming district of L'Amaroux

places.name: Hockey Hall of Fame
places.description: Unique to Toronto, and featuring the Stanley Cup, interactive exhibits, shows, and the finest collection of hockey artifacts in the world.

places.name: HTO Park
places.description: Facing the inner harbour with Toronto Island Park in clear viewing, HTO Park includes an urban beach which is decorated with yellow umbrellas and Muskoka chairs.

places.name: Humber Arboretum
places.description: Located nearby the West Humber River Valley, the Humber Arboretum offers trails through environmentally-rich areas like forests, and wetlands.

places.name: Humber Bay Park West (Humber Bay Butterfly Habitat)
places.description: Located at a waterfront park at the mouth of Mimico Creek, the Humber Bay Butterfly Habitat is focused on providing habitat for an array of native butterfly species.

places.name: Isabel Bader Theatre
places.description: Located at the University of Toronto, this multi-purpose venue seats 500 patrons whether it be for a lecture, workshop, or a theatrical production.

places.name: James Garden Park
places.description: Former estate gardens located in Toronto's west end that include rare trees, spring-fed pools, and other seasonal displays.

places.name: Kew Gardens Park
places.description: Located in The Beaches, Kew Gardens act as one of Toronto's most popular picnic grounds while having access to the boardwalk on the lakeshore.

places.name: Koerner Hall (at the Telus Centre for Performance and Learning)
places.description: Koerner Hall is a 1,135 seat venue to provide excellent acoustic sounds for all genres of music in its "shoebox" designed venue.

places.name: Little Canada
places.description: This attraction is an immersive joruney through the sights, sounds and wonder of Canada on a miniature scale.

places.name: Mackenzie House
places.hours: Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: Mackenzie House is the restored home of William Lyon Mackenzie, Toronto's first Mayor. It is one of 10 museums operated by the City of Toronto.

places.name: Marie Curtis Park East Beach
places.description: Located at the mouth of Etobicoke Creek near the foot of Forty-Second Street. Most users of this beach come from the bordering Long Branch community.

places.name: Massey Hall
places.description: Declared a heritage building in the 1970s, this live events venue acts as a performance venue for various artists.

places.name: Medieval Times Dinner and Tournament
places.description: A family dinner theatre featuring staged medieval-style games, sword-fighting, and jousting performed by a cast of actors and horses.

places.name: Mel Lastman Square
places.description: A public park featuring 20,000 square feet of open space, a garden court, an outdoor amphitheatre, fountains and a reflecting pool.

places.name: Meridian Arts Centre (formerly Toronto Centre for the Arts)
places.description: This venue features three unique stages to house a multitude of concerts, shows and events.

places.name: Meridian Hall (formerly Sony Centre for the Performing Arts)
places.description: Meridian Hall is a performing arts venue with a range of events that include concerts, dance, and much more.

places.name: Montgomery's Inn
places.hours: Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: A museum that was once a historic home, visitors can delve into the lifestyle of a 19th century Irish farm family with access to the bedrooms, kitchen wing and much more.

places.name: Museum of Illusions Toronto
places.description: The Museum of Illusions offers a wide array of mind-bending exhibits and optical illusions.

places.name: Mysteriously Yours Mystery Dinner Theatre
places.description: Mysteriously Yours. Mystery Dinner Theatre is a murder mystery dinner theatre located in Downtown Toronto.

places.name: Native Earth Performing Arts & Aki Studio
places.description: Native Earth Performing Arts is a theatre company devoted to the artistic expression of the Indigenous experience. Located in Daniels Spectrum.

places.name: Old City Hall
places.description: Old City Hall is a landmark building that was used as Toronto's second City Hall and is a great example of beautiful architecture. Today, it is used as a courthouse.

places.name: Onsite Gallery at OCAD U
places.description: Onsite [at] OCAD U provides the opportunity and space of an art gallery to exhibit students contemporary work.

places.name: Osgoode Hall
places.description: Constructed in the 19th century, Osgoode Hall acts as the judicial landmark of Toronto, with institutions like the Ontario Court of Appeal, the Law Society of Upper Canada, and the Divisional Court of the Superior Court of Justice.

places.name: Princess of Wales Theatre
places.description: Owned by Mirvish Productions. The Princess of Wales Theatre opened in 1993 and is the home of many famous theatrical productions

places.name: Queen Elizabeth Theatre
places.description: Located at Exhibition Place, the Queen Elizabeth Theatre is an auditorium that is the venue for various entertainment events

places.name: Queen's Park: Legislative Assembly of Ontario
places.description: A variety of free tour options are available all year round to visit Ontarios historic Legislative Building (iconic sandstone Richardson Romanesque style building, completed in 1893).

places.name: Randolph Centre for the Arts
places.description: The historic Randolph Theatre is a 500-seat theatre located in a former Gothic revival style church.

places.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
places.description: Canadas largest aquarium. Interactive attractions feature over 5.7 million litres of water and more than 16,000 marine animals.

places.name: Riverdale Park (East and West)
places.description: A Toronto park that is great for all seasons. Riverdale Park West has three multipurpose sport fields, seven tennis courts, an outdoor ice rink, two baseball diamonds, and much more.

places.name: Rosetta McClain Gardens
places.description: The Rosetta McClain Gardens is a great place to safely see the Scarborough Bluffs and has beautiful rose gardens. There are signs available in braille, textured paths, raised planters, and a ramp to ensure accessibility.

places.name: Rouge Beach Park
places.description: One of Toronto's designated swimming beaches, Rouge Beach has two distinct areas a white sand beach and a marsh habitat.

places.name: Rouge Valley Conservation Centre
places.description: The Centre focuses on environmental restoration and research while also offering interpretive walks and educational programs for the public.

places.name: Roy Thomson Hall
places.description: Opened in 1982, Roy Thomson Hall is home of the Toronto Symphony Orchestra and the Toronto Mendelssohn Choir.

places.name: Royal Alexandra Theatre
places.description: Owned by Mirvish Productions. The Royal Alexandra Theatre built in beaux-arts architectural style in 1907. It is home to numerous performances and performers.

places.name: Royal Conservatory of Music
places.description: The Toronto Conservatory of Music was founded in 1886.

places.name: Sankofa Square
places.description: Yonge-Dundas Square is one of the city's largest public squares. It is located directly across from the Toronto Eaton Centre. The square is home to free movie screenings, concerts, shows and exhibits.

places.name: Sarah and Chaim Neuberger Holocaust Education Centre
places.description: The Sarah and Chaim Neuberger Holocaust Education Centre provides all its visitors a complete understanding of the Holocaust.30, 000 students pass through its doors during educational trips.

places.name: Scarborough Museum
places.description: The Scarborough Museum and its gardens are located within Thomson Memorial Park.It is one of 10 museums operated by the City of Toronto.The Museum looks back on the story of Scarborough's roots and history.

places.name: Scarborough Village Theatre
places.description: Theatre Scarborough is an umbrella organization consisting of Scarborough Music Theatre, Scarborough Players, and Scarborough Theatre Guild. Performances take place at the Scarborough Village Community Centre.

places.name: Soulpepper Theatre Company
places.description: Soulpepper is a not-for-profit theatre company that offers plays and concerts with a focus on training and youth projects.

places.name: Spadina Museum
places.hours: Mon 11am to 5pm; Tue 11am to 5pm; Wed 11am to 5pm; Thu 11am to 5pm; Fri 11am to 5pm; Sat 11am to 5pm; Sun 11am to 5pm
places.description: Operated by the City of Toronto, the Spadina Museum is a historic manor house that allows visitors to learn about the history and architecture of late 19th century to early 20th century Toronto.

places.name: St. James Park
places.description: A large green space, home to a Victorian garden, live performances, and is a popular spot for photos. The park is adjacent to historic St. James Cathedral.

places.name: St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts
places.description: Home to two theatres, the Bluma Appel Theatre and the Jane Mallett Theatre, the St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts is the home to various artistic and public events.

places.name: Steam Whistle Brewery
places.costNote: Free to visit. Paid tours and tastings.
places.description: A microbrewery located in downtown Toronto, Steam Whistle Brewery produces a premium pale lager composed of only four ingredients.

places.name: Sugar Beach Park
places.description: Sugar Beach is one of Toronto's urban beach parks. Famous for its pink umbrellas and Muskoka chairs.

places.name: Sunnyside Beach
places.description: One of Toronto's designated swimming beaches, Sunnyside Beach provides rowers and paddlers calm waters with an offshore break wall.

places.name: Taras H. Shevchenko Museum
places.description: The Taras H. Shevchenko Museum is the home to exhibitions dedicated to the contribution of Ukrainians in Canada and the life of famed writer Taras Shevchenko.

places.name: Tarragon Theatre
places.description: The Tarragon Theatre is a performing arts centre notable for the development of playwrights. Over 170 works have premiered at the theatre.

places.name: Textile Museum of Canada
places.costNote: Small admission fee. Check the website.
places.description: With more than 13,000 objects from more than 200 countries and regions, the Textile Museum of Canada celebrates cultural diversity through traditional fabrics, garments, carpets and related artifacts such as beadwork and basketry.

places.name: The 48th Highlanders Museum
places.description: This museum is dedicated to one of Canada's famous military regiments. The museum holds historical artifacts dating from Victorian Toronto in 1891, when the 48th Highlanders was formed, to the present day.

places.name: The Danforth Music Hall
places.description: The Music Hall boasts new theatre seats, state-of-art sound and lighting and a completely renovated backstage area.

places.name: The Distillery Historic District
places.description: A pedestrian-only historic area that represents the largest and best preserved collection of Victorian Industrial Architecture in North America. The refurbished warehouses are now home to restaurants, bars, galleries, studios, and a theatre.

places.name: The Image Centre
places.description: The RIC is dedicated to the public exhibition, research, study and teaching of photography including, installation art and film and media.

places.name: The Japan Foundation
places.description: A cultural establishment aiming towards effective development of its international cultural exchange programs in Japanese arts and cultural exchange.

places.name: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
places.description: Dedicated to contemporary art, the Power Plant is a free public gallery located at the Harbourfront Centre.

places.name: The Second City
places.description: Second City produces premiere comedy performances and operates a training centre.

places.name: The Theatre Centre
places.description: The Theatre Centre supports artists who wish to develop works of an experimental or alternative nature. All their artists embrace the visual arts, music, dance and new media.

places.name: The Village Players
places.description: The Village Playhouse a non-profit theatre group that opened its doors in 1974 and has since produced plays such as Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, Amadeus and Dial 'M' For Murder.

places.name: Theatre Passe Muraille
places.description: Theatre Passe Muraille was Canadas original alternative theatre company. 600 Canadian plays have been produced since the company was founded in 1968.

places.name: Thompson Landry Gallery - Stone Building & Cooperage Space
places.description: The Thompson Landry Gallery is spread out over 6,000 square feet and showcases artwork from internationally acclaimed contemporary Quebec artists. The gallery opened in 2009 and is situated within the Distillery District's Cooperage Building.

places.name: TIFF Bell Lightbox
places.costNote: Free to enter. Pay per film.
places.description: The TIFF Bell Lightbox is the home of the Toronto International Film Festival and a year-round destination for unique screenings, themed festivals, and exhibitions. It also houses two restaurants.

places.name: Todmorden Mills Heritage Site
places.description: Todmorden Mills Heritage Site is situated within the Don Valley and is located beside a 9.2 hectare wildflower preserve. It features historic buildings such as the Brewery building and the Papermill theatre and gallery.

places.name: Toronto Botanical Gardens and Edwards Gardens
places.description: Located at the stunning Edwards Gardens, Toronto Botanical Garden features award-winning themed gardens and an indoor education/interpretation facility.

places.name: Toronto City Hall and Nathan Phillips Square
places.description: Toronto's City Hall is one of Toronto's best known and visited landmarks. Nathan Phillips Square located directly in front of City Hall, is the site of the iconic Toronto sign, concerts, farmers' markets, and iconic events.

places.name: Toronto Metropolitan University Theatre (formerly known as Ryerson Theatre)
places.description: Ryerson Theatre is home to various productions which includes concerts, film presentations, and Ryerson Theatre and Fashion Schools productions.

places.name: Toronto Railway Museum
places.costNote: Small admission fee. Check the website.
places.description: The Toronto Railway Museum encompasses the Canadian Pacific Railway John Street Roundhouse at Roundhouse Park and features a restored turntable, a number of trains and the 1896 Canadian Pacific Don Station.

places.name: Toronto Sculpture Garden
places.description: Since 1981 this small urban park has featured contemporary sculpture installations by various artists.

places.name: Toronto Zoo
places.description: The Toronto Zoo is one of the largest zoos in the world at 287 hectares (710 acres) and is known for interactive education and conservation activities. It is currently home to 2 giant pandas, and more than 5,000 animals representing over 500 species.

places.name: Toronto's First Post Office

places.name: Trinity Square

places.name: Black Creek at Weston Rd.
places.address: Humber Blvd. N. and Weston Rd.
places.description: Toronto's geography was shaped by repeated glaciations over thousands of years and the rapid draining of Lake Iroquois that created steep ridges and depressions on the landscape, which resulted in the abundance of ravines and rivers running throughout the city today.

places.name: Mount Dennis Eco Mural
places.description: This colourful mural, designed and painted by Alex Bacon (Alexander Lazich) and Christina Mazzulla, depicts an egret, an owl and a red-winged black bird. Inspired by the nature themes in the pollinator mural across the street, the mural reflects the local wildlife of the Mount Dennis and Humber River area.

places.name: Eglinton Flats
places.description: The Eglinton Flats cover three of the four corners at Eglinton Avenue and Jane Street, including the Eglinton Flats Park, Fergy Brown Park (named after former Mayor of York and Mount Dennis resident) and Gladhurst Park. Collectively, the three parks make up Toronto's largest regional sports field facility.

places.name: High Water Mark
places.description: High Water Mark is an art installation by Robert Sprachman commissioned by the City of Toronto in 2011. It highlights the importance of the Don River and its water, reminding people that the water can be both tranquil and powerful.

places.name: Salmon Jumping Point
places.description: Look at the river and you will see rocky ramps built by Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA). These structures help provide a passage for jumping fish such as salmon.

places.name: Ancient Lake Iroquois
places.description: When the last glaciers retreated from Toronto between 13,000 and 14,000 years ago, deep layers of till, silt and clay were left behind. Water levels rose significantly, creating Lake Iroquois. As glaciers retreated, land levels slowly rose, water eventually drained through the St.

places.name: West Don River
places.description: The West Don River begins in Vaughan near Keele Street and Kirby Road. It flows south from the Oak Ridges Moraine by way of G. Ross Lord Park, passing through Earl Bales Park, Hoggs Hollow at Yonge Street, Glendon Forest behind York University to this location.

places.name: Don River Valley
places.description: One of Toronto's most remarkable features is the 400-metre-wide Don Valley, formed 12,000 years ago when the area was covered in ice. As the climate warmed, glacier meltwater eroded deep valleys, forming several rivers in the area.

places.name: Pottery Road Underpass Mural
places.address: Pottery Rd. underpass at Don Valley Pkwy
places.description: Artist Drew Mosley's mural, on the south pillars of the Pottery Road Underpass, celebrates the wildlife of the Don Valley area. The artist used fantastical imagery to illustrate and animate the animals, resulting in a whimsical and beautiful piece, created with support from StreetARToronto.

places.name: Todmorden Mills Wildflower Preserve
places.description: The wildflower preserve was established in 1991 to restore nine hectares of the Todmorden Mills area to its pre-settlement natural condition, including wetlands and forest areas. Rapid industrial and residential developments throughout the 19th and 20th centuries had destroyed much of this natural landscape.

places.name: Chester Hill Lookout
places.address: Chester Hill Rd. at Thorncliffe Ave.
places.description: Visit Chester Hill for a breathtaking view of the Toronto skyline. This hidden lookout reveals the juxtaposition of nature and urban development in Toronto. From here you can see the Don River, the natural views of the surrounding forest and the wetlands, with the downtown skyline as a backdrop.

places.name: Pods Through Time Mosaic Mural
places.description: This mosaic mural is a celebration of the Coxwell and Danforth neighbourhood, recognizing its East York history, its current community and culture, and its future potential.

places.name: Alleyway of Dreams
places.description: This somewhat hidden urban gallery features a number of murals on the back walls and garages of local businesses. This creative initiative was championed by the Danforth Village BIA, supporting the long-term community art project started by local residents Mark Kerwin and Sarosh Anwar.

places.name: Taylor Massey Trail
places.description: The 3.5 kilometre Taylor Massey Trail follows the southeastern section of the 16 kilometre long Taylor Massey Creek, a tributary of the Don River, named for the Taylor and Massey families, each of which had a significant historical impact on the area.

places.name: Forks of the Don
places.address: Lower Don Recreation Trail at Don Mills Rd.
places.description: Follow the Lower Don River Trail to where it passes beneath Don Mills Road, to see where the West Don and East Don meet to form the Lower Don River. The intersection of the Don Rivers two main tributaries is known as the Forks of the Don and is a significant geographical feature of this area.

places.name: Then & Now Mural
places.description: Then & Now, created by artists Jim Bravo and Lula Lumaj, focuses on themes of history, nature and urbanization. The mural depicts a precolonial historical scene with three First Nations people crossing a creek, in reference to the historic creek that ran south down Linsmore Avenue all the way to Ashbridges Bay.

places.name: Women in the Walls
places.description: Women in the Walls All Female Street Art Jam was a SPARK Project of the 2017 Cultural Hotspot in partnership with artist Monica Wickeler and StreetARToronto that featured 18 women painting murals through the weekend-long live paint event. On the side of 1460 Gerrard St. E.

places.name: Project Picasso
places.description: Located in the Green P Parking lot behind the large Zhong Hua Men Archway, this Asian-inspired mural project was initiated by Toronto Police 55 Division, working with artists and youth from Riverdale Collegiate Institute to combat graffiti.

places.name: Great Wall of China, China
places.description: Where else can you see the wonders of the world in a few city blocks? The New7Wonders of the World project was initiated by StreetARToronto in partnership with multiple community organizations. This is one of a series of large-scale murals spread out around East Chinatown, painted by 20 artists and students.

places.name: The Gatehouse Transformational Healing Garden
places.description: The Healing Garden was created in 2014 by The Gatehouse staff and community volunteers. It is a place for meditation and contemplation.

places.name: Wetland Lookout
places.address: Colonel Samuel Smith Park at North Creek
places.description: The wetland lookout was originally built in 1995. It is a popular place for bird watchers and nature education programs. It was rebuilt in 2015 and it provides access to observe mature trees, marshes and birds.

places.name: Elmcrest Creek
places.description: Elmcrest Creek continues through Bloordale Park and north to Burnhamthorpe Road, south of Centennial Park. Below Bloor Street West, the creek path connects with Neilson Park Creative Centre. The creek is a tributary of Etobicoke Creek.

places.name: The Old Swimming Hole
places.description: The site that inspired this piece of art by John Kuna was located on Willow Dale Farm on Mimico Creek, originally at the site of a functioning sawmill frequented by village youth. The mill stood beside the creek in what is now Islington Golf Course, down below the intersection of Burnhamthorpe Road and Mattice Road.

places.name: Toboggan Hill
places.description: Toboggan Hill is one of three murals with the "children at play" theme by John Kuna. The inspiration for this mural came from a photo in the Islington archives of Montgomery's Inn.

places.name: Flight of the Passenger Pigeon
places.description: The mural, painted by John Kuna, pays homage to the now extinct passenger pigeon. It depicts a pigeon in flight against an abstract background. It was designed so that as the viewer observes the mural from one end to the other, the bird appears to be fading, reflecting the extinction of the species.

places.name: Winter Crafts & Cozy Treats: Holiday Season at Scarborough Museum
places.description: Celebrate light, connection and community in a cozy historic setting each weekend. Enjoy hands-on family-friendly activities centered on food, culture and storytelling. Create festive winter crafts, gather around the fire and enjoy warm beverages and freshly baked treats prepared on the historic cast-iron stove.

places.name: Mud Pies: Scarborough Arts Annual Juried Exhibition
places.address: Cedar Ridge Creative Centre, 225 Confederation Dr
places.description: Scarborough Arts holds their Annual Juried Exhibition as a showcase of work by local and emerging artists in Scarborough. This year, get your hands dirty with Mud Pies. Inspired by the childlike sense of wonder, whimsy and play we often find in our earliest encounters with the natural world, Mud Pies asks us to consider our relationship with soil and the earth beneath our feet.

places.name: Disney and Pixar's Finding Nemo
places.address: Young People's Theatre, 165 Front St E
places.description: Make your holidays merry with an enchanting family adventure! This splashy musical adaptation of the beloved Pixar film celebrates the love between parents and children in a vivid underwater world. When Nemo, a spirited clownfish with a “lucky fin" is captured by a diver, his cautious father, Marlin, embarks on an epic rescue mission across the ocean.

places.name: FOOD TOURS: Cozy Bites in Old Town Toronto
places.address: St Lawrence Market, 95 Front St E, Toronto
places.description: Take a delicious detour through Old Town Toronto this fall! Presented by Old Town Toronto BIA, Eat More Food Tours invites you to explore this historic neighbourhood through its local flavours, fascinating stories and seasonal charm. Wander along a charming, walkable route through streets awash in autumn colour. Stop to sample local flavours and culinary treasures at the iconic St.

places.name: First Wednesday Night Free at the AGO
places.address: Art Gallery of Ontario, 317 Dundas St W
places.description: Enjoy the galleries at night. Please dress for the weather as the queue for entrance begins outside the AGO. Pack light as wait times for coat check may be longer than usual. Bags larger than a small purse, including backpacks and totes must be left at coat check for a fee. Please refrain from bringing oversized bags.

places.name: Cowboys and Wallflowers Exhibition
places.address: Assembly Hall Gallery, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr
places.description: Immerse in collages that blend iconic imagery and wit to challenge gender norms and domestic expectations. Despite shifting gender dynamics, her work highlights ongoing struggles over household roles. Each piece is meticulously handmade from vintage materials dating 1800s–1970s by Danielle Colle.

places.name: Saturday Farmers' Market
places.address: St. Lawrence North Market, 92 Front St E, Toronto
places.description: Visit the Saturday Farmers' Market in the newly redeveloped St. Lawrence Market North building. Discover seasonal produce, baked goods, meats, cheeses, flowers and pantry staples from local vendors all under one roof.

places.name: Held by Anne Michaels - By the Lake Book Club
places.address: Assembly Hall, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr
places.description: Held, by 2024 Scotiabank Giller Prize winner Anne Michaels, is a luminous, fragmented novel about love, memory, and the reverberations of war across generations. Beginning on a First World War battlefield, the narrative moves through time and place to explore how desire and grief endure beyond a single lifetime.

places.name: Sketch Party
places.description: Each month we're partying HARD and bringing the best sketch comedy this city has to offer, from the hottest up and coming troupes to long time fan favourite troupes and solo acts. Get ready for a wild night of expecting the unexpected and, of course, sketch comedy. Bring your best party trick and enjoy the vibes. There ain't no party like a S-KETCH PARTY!

places.name: SignFest Toronto 2026
places.address: North York Memorial Community Hall, 5110 Yonge Street North York, ON M2N 5V7
places.description: This is a free public festival celebrating Deaf culture, sign language, accessibility, and inclusion. The festival features a free daytime expo with vendors, exhibitors, organizations, presentations, entertainment, and networking opportunities.

places.name: Molly Steels: I Am/Was/Always
places.description: The philosopher Diana Prokofyeva considers a photograph to be a phenomenon that exists as a way to avoid death by copying a moment and suspending it within time - a way to be between two worlds:, the living and the dead. She suggests that a photograph gives confidence of existence, a way to state, “Here I am and was, and always shall have been.”.

places.name: Tanya Marcuse: Portent
places.description: Tanya Marcuse’s multichannel video Portent presents ominous scenes of the natural world: trees swaying in the wind, vapour rising from volcanic fumaroles, icy branches illuminated by flickering light, and other small disturbances that hint at forces beyond our understanding.

places.name: A Spore on its Journey
places.description: Huan Chen transforms native fungi and lichen into a powerful metaphor for the immigrant experience, telling stories of heritage, struggle, adaptation and new beginnings. Through striking imagery, the work also reflects on human impact on natural habitats and the cultural shifts shaping urban life. Don’t miss this thought-provoking installation that connects nature, identity and community in surprising ways.

places.name: New Vistas
places.address: Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery, 399 The West Mall
places.description: Celebrate emerging voices in art at this annual exhibition, developed in partnership between the City of Toronto and Humber Polytechnic’s Arts Administration & Cultural Management Program. Showcasing early-career artists with focus on IBPOC, persons with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQIAS+, New Vistas highlights bold, fresh perspectives. Witness the creativity shaping the next generation of artists and arts leaders.

places.name: 74th Open Juried Exhibit
places.address: Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery, 399 The West Mall
places.description: Colour and Form Society presents an exhibit opportunity for their artists to showcase a myriad of talent, and for non-members to be juried into membership of the organization. The Colour and Form Society was established in 1952 and has played a significant role in the cultural mosaic of Canada—promoting diversity, creative freedom, and independence in art. Reception: November 1, 2–4 p.m.

places.name: A Christmas Carol
places.address: The Fleck at Harbourfront Centre Theatre, 231 Queens Quay W
places.description: Dickens’s timeless holiday story of transformation, kindness and human connection. This fresh adaptation by Tim Carroll brings Charles Dickens’s world to life through inventive puppetry, towering ghosts that fill the stage, traditional carols and audience participation with spirited sing-alongs.

places.name: Jazz at the Columbus Centre
places.address: Joseph D. Carrier Art Gallery, 901 Lawrence Ave W
places.description: Celebrate the richness, diversity and enduring appeal of jazz. Back by popular demand, enjoy ive unforgettable concerts celebrating the richness, diversity, and enduring appeal of jazz.

places.name: Places That Stayed: Youth Photography Exhibit
places.address: East Scarborough Storefront, 4040 Lawrence Ave E
places.description: Discover Kingston-Galloway-Orton Park (KGO) through the eyes of local youth in this outdoor photography exhibit. Created as part of a youth placemaking and photography project, the exhibit features photographs documenting the places and spaces that make the neighbourhood unique, from familiar gathering spots and busy streets to quiet corners, overlooked landscapes, parks, and community spaces.

places.name: Locke Library Talk
places.description: Toronto has one of the largest urban forests in the world. Join the City of Toronto for an in-library presentation on this amazing natural habitat that reaches all corners of Toronto. We’ll discuss what makes the urban forest so special and share tools to help you explore and understand it better.

places.name: Downsview Park Merchants Market
places.description: Downsview Park Merchants Market is one of Toronto’s vibrant weekend destinations, offering a dynamic indoor marketplace experience for shoppers of all ages. Located in North York, the market features a diverse mix of local vendors offering clothing, accessories, home goods, beauty products, electronics, toys, collectibles, gifts, fresh produce, specialty items, and incredible deals.

places.name: The Stop Farmers' Market @ Wychwood Barns Park
places.description: Featuring 35+ weekly vendors, the market brings together local farmers, food producers, and neighbours to increase access to healthy food in ways that build community. A program of The Stop Community Food Centre, the market supports both emerging and established small-scale producers while strengthening a resilient local food economy through responsibly grown and produced food.

places.name: Immersion Festival
places.description: Join us for a celebration of Canadian cultural life for audiences and a sought-after performance and networking opportunity for renowned and aspiring artists, with three distinct stage performances, twelve workshops, a dance education roundtable, and community gatherings. Performances and workshops are open to all!

places.name: Allan Gardens Saturday Farmers' Market
places.description: Celebrate local food, community, and sustainable agriculture. Discover fresh produce, artisanal products, and small-scale producers - all while connecting with the people who grow and create them.We invite you to come meet the vendors, discover new favourites, and taste the heart of your community!

places.name: Sunday Variety Market
places.address: St. Lawrence Market (Big White Tent), 125 The Esplanade, Toronto
places.description: Get ready for the ultimate weekend treasure hunt! The Sunday Variety Market is now open every Saturday and Sunday, bringing the city’s biggest and most exciting market experience to life each week.

places.name: Toronto Sunday Market
places.address: The Parkdale Hall, 1605 Queen St W
places.description: A vibrant weekly market celebrating local creators, delicious food & community Handmade Goods • Antiques • Vintage • Family-friendly Support local. Shop small. Eat fresh.

places.name: Beach Photo Club Exhibition
places.address: Clark Centre for the Arts, 191 Guildwood Pkwy
places.description: Enjoy this photography exhibition by a diverse group of artists as they present their unique interpretations of our world, from realistic to abstract, including techniques such as macro photography, intentional movement and digital compositing. This collection promises a rich visual experience that reflects the wide-ranging creativity of Beach Photo Club members.

places.name: Dancing Blossoms Installation
places.address: Clark Centre for the Arts, 191 Guildwood Pkwy
places.description: Delight in Paula Hartmann's Dancing Blossoms, a kinetic installation composed of dozens of delicate paper mobiles suspended in air, evoking the quiet poetry of spring trees swaying in the wind. Crafted from featherlight paper and fine wire, each mobile captures a fleeting moment of bloom, movement, and renewal.

places.name: Geoffrey James | Ancient and Modern: Selected Panoramas
places.address: Stephen Bulger Gallery, 1356 Dundas St W
places.description: The Stephen Bulger Gallery is pleased to present there second solo exhibition of work by Geoffrey James, one of Canada’s pre-eminent photographers. James’s panoramic photographs explore the relationship between people and the landscapes they create, shape, and transform. He became known for using a panoramic camera to photograph gardens, parks, cities, mines, and other human-made environments.

places.name: Lakeshore Dance Series: Premiere Dance Presentations
places.address: Assembly Hall, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr
places.description: Encounter an elevated arts experience this fall featuring two compelling dance works in one exhilarating programme: CON by KINAJ and Unrequited by Atri Nundy, plus guest appearances by dancers from Sync&Flow and Sampradaya Dance Academy. CON - Vietnamese for "child" - is a cross-genre Hip Hop and Contemporary work moving through báo hiếu, the generational debt of gratitude.

places.name: Kensington Market ‘Taste the World’ Food Tour Fall 2026
places.description: Explore Kensington Market with the tour that started it all! As the original food tour of one of Toronto’s quirkiest neighbourhoods, you will get to enjoy beyond the tourist traps to family-run shops, hidden counters, and must-try bites most visitors walk right past. Skip the lines and taste local favourites from around the world, from handmade Tibetan dumplings to flaky Jamaican patties.

places.name: Richard Avedon: Immortal: Portraits of Aging
places.description: For nearly half a century, celebrated American photographer Richard Avedon confronted one of portraiture’s enduring taboos: aging. From his earliest years at Harper’s Bazaar, Avedon broke with the conventions of idealized celebrity portraiture, revealing the marks of time on his subjects’ faces with unsparing clarity.

places.name: Toronto Comedy All Stars
places.address: The Second City Toronto, 110 Harbour St
places.description: Catch the hottest standups from Toronto’s world class comedy scene! Featuring comedians seen on Prime, Netflix Is A Joke Fest, Just For Laughs, CBC, Crave, Hulu and more. Discover the next wave of comedy stars at the iconic Second City stage, famous for launching legends like Catherine O'Hara, Eugene Levy, Mike Myers & many more!

places.name: Agincourt Library Invasive Plants Talk
places.description: Join City of Toronto staff for a presentation on invasive plants commonly found around homes in Toronto. Learn how to identify these species, understand their impact and effectively manage them. You’ll also get tips on supporting local biodiversity through enhancing native habitats. Perfect for gardeners, homeowners and anyone interested in urban ecology. All are welcome. No registration necessary.

places.name: Mixology: Cocktail Class
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: Come along to our Cocktails Masterclass! This is a great beginner class for people 19+ looking to improve their bartending skills! During this 90-minutes class you will get to learn how to mix three different cocktails. Most of the components for the cocktails will be pre-made by the chef instructor, so you can get right to the fun mixing and tasting part.

places.name: International Architectural Design Competition 2026-2027: Persian Garden Suite
places.description: This international architectural competition invites participants to design a Persian Garden Suite pavilion in Toronto.

places.name: Yesterday. Today. Forever.
places.address: Mount Pleasant Cemetery, 375 Mount Pleasant Road
places.description: Walk through a series of artistic and interpretive installations across ten cemetery sites and several funeral centres.

places.name: Ho, Ho, Holiday Cookie Baking
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: Join us for our Holiday Cookie Baking Class! In this three-hour, hands-on class, you'll learn how to make three festive holiday cookies: Linzer Cookies, Thumbprint Cookies, and Chocolate Crinkle Cookies. Our talented chefs will guide you through each recipe, sharing tips and techniques along the way. The best part? You'll take home the yummy cookies that you will have made!

places.name: Benedict Sheehan’s ‘Ukrainian War Requiem’: The National Tour
places.description: The Axios Men’s Ensemble, in celebration of their historic Juno award, for Classical Album of the Year (Large Ensemble) for the recording of Benedict Sheehan’s Ukrainian War Requiem, have announced a national tour this November.

places.name: A Very Merry Magic Show
places.description: This holiday season, BenTastic and Magic Mel take the stage together for a Christmas celebration full of festive cheer, wonder, and magical surprises! Packed with laughter, wonder, and plenty of audience participation, this high-energy show blends dazzling illusions, hilarious comedy, and heartwarming holiday spirit.

places.name: Intro to Bread: Challah
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: Join us for our Challah Class! This class is great for absolute beginners! And you will achieve all this in just ONE day! Spend two hours with our talented chef to learn the art of making Challah. Using pre-measured ingredients, you'll mix your own dough from scratch while learning the techniques and skills that will give you the confidence to tackle bread recipes at home.

places.name: Champagne & Macarons New Years Eve!
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: A beginner-friendly experience where guests learn to bake, pipe, fill and assemble Parisian macarons while enjoying champagne. They will explore macaronage, meringue techniques and proper macaron storage, then take home approximately 20 handmade macarons in a provided transport box. Guests also receive the macaron and Swiss meringue buttercream recipes by email before class.

places.name: New Years Eve Celebration Cake Class
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: Join us in decorating your own New Years' Eve cake. This is two hour class is perfect for beginners! We will bake the cakes for you and make buttercream in advance, so you can get to the super fun decorating part.

places.name: The Glenn Gould School Chamber Opera Barber’s A Hand of Bridge and Bernstein’s Trouble in Tahiti
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: This season’s offering will be a double bill of Samuel Barber’s A Hand of Bridge, a poignant miniature opera that reveals the hidden thoughts of four bridge players during a seemingly ordinary card game, and Leonard Bernstein’s Trouble in Tahiti, a jazz-infused one-act opera depicting a day in the life of a troubled married couple living in 1950s suburbia. Conducted by Jennifer Tung and directed by Mario Pacheco.

places.name: Punch Brothers
places.description: Punch Brothers, formed by mandolinist Chris Thile in 2006, is known for pushing the boundaries of acoustic music. In addition to Thile, the band currently comprises guitarist Chris Eldridge, bassist Paul Kowert, banjoist Noam Pikelny, and violinist Brittany Haas. Punch Brothers has garnered critical acclaim, including a Grammy for Best Folk Album for All Ashore (2018).

places.name: Aga Khan Master Musicians
places.description: Creating music inspired by their own deep roots in the cultures of the Middle East and Mediterranean Basin, South Asia, Central Asia, and China.

places.name: Kids PA Day Baking Camp
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: Do your kids need a creative baking outlet? Sign up your children to bake and decorate a variety of delicious treats while having fun!

places.name: Indigenous Beading Workshop: Poppy
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: In honour of Remembrance Day and National Indigenous Veterans Day, join Natalie Ortiz for a meaningful afternoon of beading, reflection, and remembrance. In this hands-on workshop, participants will create a beautiful beaded poppy while learning about the significance of poppies as symbols of remembrance and the important contributions and sacrifices of Indigenous veterans.

places.name: Canadian Disability Tech Summit
places.description: Be a part of the national conversation shaping the future of disability innovation, assistive technology, and accessibility in Canada. The Canadian Disability Tech Summit 2026 brings together leaders from across the accessibility ecosystem for a full day of industry insights, emerging technology showcases, strategic networking, and cross-sector collaboration.

places.name: The Suite Life
places.address: Trinity- St. Paul's Centre, 427 Bloor St. West, Toronto, On,M5S 1X7
places.description: Violinist Irmina Trynkos, praised by BBC Music Magazine as "an intense and charismatic new star," takes centre stage for the Toronto premiere of Claudia Montero's Violin Concerto; a Latin Grammy-winning work heard in Toronto for the very first time.

places.name: Exhibition: "Returning to Ourselves and Michael Massie: now and then"
places.description: Please join us at the 'Returning to Ourselves - Rebecca Baird and Kenny Alvin Baird: A Retrospective of Art and Design by Cree Métis Siblings'. Curated by Lisa Deanne Smith. This exhibit presents over 40 years of transformative work by Rebecca Baird and Kenny Alvin Baird. The exhibition spans sculpture, painting and traditional material practices, alongside interior design and more.

places.name: Oscar Peterson Program
places.description: Enjoy student concerts featuring solo and chamber works and the Oscar Peterson Program Orchestra conducted by Artistic Director Colin Clarke.

places.name: John Beasley’s Unlimited Miles: Miles Davis at 100
places.description: Under the direction of Grammy Award-winning pianist, composer, and arranger John Beasley, star‑studded musicians Marcus Strickland on saxophone, Sean Jones on trumpet, Ben Williams on bass, and Terreon Gully on drums delve into the visionary spirit and boundless creativity of Miles Davis.

places.name: Royal Conservatory Orchestra with conductor Tania Miller with Anna Yin, violin
places.description: Canadian conductor Tania Miller has distinguished herself as a dynamic interpreter, musician, and innovator.

places.name: New Music Concerts: Blackout In Vain
places.description: For 55 years, New Music Concerts has been one of Canada’s leading forces in contemporary music. Widely hailed as the first masterpiece of the 21st century, Georg Friedrich Haas’s in vain is one of the most admired works of our time. Performed by a group of Toronto’s top professional musicians, this extraordinary piece transforms sound into a living, shifting landscape of microtonal colour.

places.name: Vicky Chow Plays Philip Glass
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: Vancouver-raised “monster pianist” (Time Out New York) and “one of the new stars of new music” (Los Angeles Times), Vicky Chow mesmerizes with a performance of legendary composer Philip Glass’s Piano Etudes. Philip Glass lauds Chow’s recording of his Etudes as “a highly dynamic and expressive performance. There’s a certain energy that is uniquely hers.”.

places.name: Ravi Coltrane: The John Coltrane Centennial with Ewen Farncombe and Friends
places.description: The visionary saxophonist honours his father’s legacy. Ravi Coltrane is a critically acclaimed Grammy Award-nominated saxophonist, bandleader and composer. Over the course of a twenty year career, Mr. Coltrane has worked as a sideman to many, recorded noteworthy albums for himself and others and founded a prominent independent record label, RKM.

places.name: Robi Botos and Friends
places.description: The protégé of Canadian jazz legend Oscar Peterson and RCM’s Jazz Artist in Residence returns with his mesmerizing blend of bebop, modern jazz and eastern European sounds. A three-time Juno Award-winning musician, composer and educator, Robi Botos has been hailed as one of the most diverse multi-instrumentalists of this generation.

places.name: The Robert W. and G. Ann Corcoran Concerto Competition Finals
places.description: Students of The Glenn Gould School compete for the opportunity to perform a concerto with the Royal Conservatory Orchestra during the 2027 - 28 concert season.

places.name: Bang on a Can All‑Stars: Reich and Glass at 90
places.description: The Bang on a Can All-Stars have collaborated and toured with fellow New Yorkers Philip Glass and Steve Reich for more than 30 years. This concert features Glassworks, exclusively arranged by Michael Riesman alongside Reich’s acclaimed rock-infused Electric Counterpoint for electric guitar, in honor of these two outstanding composers during their milestone 90th birthday year.

places.name: The Glenn Gould School Vocal Showcase
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: A wonderful opportunity to see the talented voice students present an evening of art songs and opera excerpts.

places.name: Dance Collection DANSE Hall of Fame
places.address: Palais Royale Ballroom, 1601 Lake Shore Blvd W
places.description: Join us in celebrating DANSE's 40th Anniversary year as we introduce this year's Hall of Fame inductees! This celebration will bring together artists, cultural leaders, donors, sponsors, and audiences from across Canada for an evening of inductions, live performances, community gathering, and delicious appetizers and beverages.

places.name: The Glenn Gould School: Barber’s A Hand of Bridge and Bernstein’s Trouble in Tahiti
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: This season’s offering will be a double bill feature. Enjoy Samuel Barber’s A Hand of Bridge, a poignant miniature opera that reveals the hidden thoughts of four bridge players during a seemingly ordinary card game. As well, listen to Leonard Bernstein’s Trouble in Tahiti, a jazz-infused one-act opera depicting a day in the life of a troubled married couple living in 1950s suburbia.

places.name: A Translucent City: Collective Memories of the Future
places.description: What do cities remember? How do our stories, relationships and experiences shape the places we call home? Drawing on community conversations, storytelling, a Sharing Circle and arts-based research, this evolving exhibition, featuring illuminated textile maps, documentary film and opportunities for public participation, explores how people connect to place and imagine urban futures.

places.name: Sex in the '80s
places.description: Old history. New rules. They haven’t seen each other since the 1980s. Now two accomplished architects are reunited in a glass-walled Toronto office tower on the eve of a high-stakes competition. Both intend to keep things strictly professional. That proves harder than expected.

places.name: Bouchara: The Light of Other Worlds
places.description: Brian Current leads Glenn Gould School students in bold contemporary music that opens imagined worlds. Enjoy pieces from Claude Vivier’s Bouchara to works by Hannah Kendall and Francis Battah. Bouchara, Vivier’s luminous work for soprano and ensemble, is widely recognized as one of his most beautiful and singular creations.

places.name: Jean‑Michel Blais
places.description: Jean-Michel Blais is a Montreal-based pianist, composer, and performer, signed to Arts & Crafts and Mercury KX (Decca).

places.name: Youth Entrepreneurship Program
places.address: Heritage Skills Development Centre, 2387 Eglinton Ave E
places.description: Do you have an idea, a passion, or the drive to build or grow your own business? The Scarborough Youth Entrepreneurship Project is offering a 10-week in-person training program designed to help you turn your ideas into reality.

places.name: Michael Massie | now and then Curatorial Tour with Alysa Procida
places.description: Discover the ideas behind this exhibit in a special curator-led tour with exhibition guest curator Alysa Procida. Through an engaging, in-depth discussion, Alysa will explore the exhibition’s curatorial vision and the creative evolution of Michael Massie’s remarkable practice.

places.name: Goodnight Desdemona (Good Morning Juliet)
places.address: Bluma Appel Theatre, 27 Front St E
places.description: A joyful comedy that flips the script on Shakespeare's most infamous heroines. To celebrate the 40th anniversary of her landmark play, acclaimed novelist and playwright Ann-Marie MacDonald steps into the spotlight as Constance Ledbelly, the overlooked academic who tumbles headlong into Shakespeare’s worlds and discovers that the heroines (and even Constance herself) may be capable of far more than anyone imagined.

places.name: Cinderella
places.address: The Winter Garden Theatre, 189 Yonge St
places.description: The classic story, turned on its heel. Think you’ve outgrown the panto? Think again. Our new take on Cinderella delivers all the glitter and spectacle of the beloved tradition with a clever, contemporary edge. Packed with infectious pop anthems, sly humour, and spectacular stagecraft, this is a holiday outing designed as much for grown-ups as it is for kids.

places.name: Lassonde Art Trail: Art + Nature Tour
places.description: Join LAT every Saturday at 12 pm or 2 pm for a drop-in Art + Nature tour led by a LAT Art Guide. These walking tours invite participants to explore the artworks along the Lassonde Art Trail while discovering the rich history, ecology, and ongoing transformation of Biidaasige Park. 12 pm - Art + Nature Tour (30 minutes, slow paced) 2 pm - Art + Nature Tour (1 hour) Meet in front of Old Fire Hall 30.

places.name: Bertrand Chamayou, Piano
places.description: Please join us for an unforgettable evening with Bertrand Chamayou, one of today’s most strikingly brilliant pianists, as he performs a program celebrating the Romantic and French repertoires! Chamayou has been recognised for his revelatory performances, at once powerfully virtuosic, imaginative and breathtakingly beautiful.

places.name: They Walked These Streets... and Answered the Call: Remembrance Installation at Fort York
places.address: Fort York National Historic Site, 250 Fort York Blvd
places.description: Torontonians answered the call to war by enlisting in the armed forces, producing munitions and equipment and by helping on the home front. This temporary installation highlights stories of the people and places along Toronto’s waterfront that shaped the war effort from 1914 to 1918 and 1939 to 1945.

places.name: Adventure of the Little Rooster
places.description: From the team that brought you The Little Circus that Could and The Philip & Lucinda Dino-Show comes a new feather of a tale! Everything changes the day the Little Rooster finds a shiny silver coin. Hilarious consequences and supreme shenanigans abound! Dazzle and delight at this retelling of this beloved folk tale performed with music, dance, puppets, circus and cabbage!

places.name: Nature Connection: Bonfire Program – food around the fire
places.description: We will be learning how to build fires, roasting some snacks and enjoying some time in the forest. This program is intended for individuals and families, all ages are welcome but those under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

places.name: Late Night at the Bata Shoe Museum
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: Enjoy our new late night hours with special craft programming new each week plus access to all current exhibitions!

places.name: Salon du Chocolat et de la Pâtisserie
places.description: Come visit a legendary global network active in 14 world capitals from Paris to Tokyo! Perfect for all sweet tooths and chocolate lovers.

places.name: Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World
places.description: Celebrate flamenco’s global transformation! Experience the vibrant evolution of flamenco, from its regional roots in Andalusia to a dynamic global art form shaped by cross-cultural exchange. This year’s lineup spans both traditional flamenco from Andalusia and innovative collaborations at the crossroads of qawwali and Persian muqam, tracing the art form’s evolution from its regional roots to a global practice.

places.name: 50 Years of Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery Exhibition - 50th Anniversary
places.address: Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery, 399 The West Mall
places.description: Discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, prints, images and paintings from City of Toronto’s Fine Art, Artifact and Archival collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

places.name: Riverside Holiday Market
places.address: Ralph Thornton Community Centre, 765 Queen St E
places.description: Bring holiday cheer and enjoy holiday activities including a Meet and Greet with Santa, live music, hot chocolate, arts and crafts and lots of local shopping. Visit website for more event perks and promos.

places.name: Curator’s Talk: Time, Labour and the Value of Beads
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World, join Director and Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadwork traditions from around the world and their role as markers of wealth, prestige, and cultural meaning.

places.name: Curator’s Talk: André Perugia
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: Step behind the scenes of the new exhibit André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled for a curator talk with Nishi Bassi.

places.name: Rachel Fenlon, soprano and piano
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: Canadian classical singer and pianist Rachel Fenlon presents deeply personal interpretations of song, performing simultaneously as vocalist and pianist in an intimate presentation.

places.name: By the Lake Book Club – 6-Event Package (2027)
places.address: Assembly Hall, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr
places.description: Presented by: City of Toronto’s Assembly Hall and Toronto Book Awards, Humber Polytechnic’s Faculty of Media, Creative Arts and Design Join leading Canadian authors as they dive into conversation about their latest books with Humber Polytechnic alumni at Assembly Hall. The 2027 lineup features the 2026 Toronto Book Award Winner, Nadja Lubiw-Hazard, Ashraf Zaghal, Tyler Pennock, Gillian Deacon and Carrianne Leung.

places.name: Taste of Downtown Yonge Beverage Tour
places.address: Meeting Point: Daon Cafe, 475 Yonge Street
places.description: Six drinks. Local cafés, tea shops, bakeries and neighbourhood hot spots. 90 minutes of discovery. Explore Downtown Yonge in a whole new way with a special beverage focus. You’ll visit a selection of 6 local cafés, tea shops, bakeries and neighbourhood hot spots, sampling six different beverages along the way.

places.name: Linocut Workshop: André Perugia Themed Tote Bag
places.costNote: Cost inclusive all materials and access to all current exhibitions.
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: Inspired by our current exhibition, André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled, step into the bold and imaginative world of André Perugia. In this hands-on linocut workshop inspired by the visionary footwear designer’s sculptural and avant-garde creations.

places.name: Rebanks Family Fellowship Concert
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: Solo and chamber works are performed by young artists on the cusp of major careers, who are enrolled in The Rebanks Family Fellowship and International Performance Residency Program at The Glenn Gould School.

places.name: Flemingdon Park Library Talk: Our Urban Forest
places.address: Flemingdon Park Library, 29 St Dennis Dr
places.description: Toronto has one of the largest urban forests in the world. Join the City of Toronto for an in-library presentation on this amazing natural habitat that reaches all corners of Toronto. We’ll talk about what makes the urban forest so special, and share tools to explore and understand it better.

places.name: The Phil and Eli Taylor Performance Academy Showcase Concert
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: Enjoy a concert by the leading young classical musicians in Canada. Hear the stars of tomorrow!

places.name: Taste of Downtown Yonge Fall Flavours: Walking Food Tour
places.description: Fall Flavours is a seasonal one-hour food tour designed especially for people who work in and around the neighbourhood.

places.name: Returning to Ourselves | Curatorial Tour with Lisa Deanne Smith
places.address: OCAD University - Onsite Gallery, 199 Richmond St W
places.description: Please join the exhibition curator for an engaging and in-depth curatorial tour of Returning to Ourselves: Rebecca Baird and Kenny Alvin Baird - A Retrospective of Art and Design by Cree Métis Siblings. Lisa Deanne Smith is Senior Curator of Onsite Gallery at OCAD University.

places.name: Academy Chamber Orchestra
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: String students from The Phil and Eli Taylor Performance Academy for Young Artists come together as the Academy Chamber Orchestra to perform a special concert.

places.name: Meow Meow: Feline Festive
places.description: Rekindle the true spirit of the holidays with the fabulous Meow Meow! The international cabaret sensation brings her singular blend of comedy, glamour, and vocal brilliance for a holiday performance like no other. Featuring a band of superb musicians, and music ranging from jazzy vintage showbiz to original and contemporary classics, this is going to be a night to remember.

places.name: Firecracker Dept Comedy Cafe
places.description: Looking for something fun to do on a Tuesday night?
