Come and see an all-women and non-binary comedy lineup, featuring a rotating cast of some of Toronto’s funniest women & non-binary comedians, showcasing a mix of stand-up, improv, sketch and more! Don't miss the laughs! It's going to be a party!

places.name: All The Cows Are Dead
places.description: This musical follows an artisan butcher who instructs his petulant and misanthropic nephew how to be more like him, leading them to discover how both are, in fact, the same. A new play with book, lyrics and music by Ben Page, directed by William Dao, featuring Mike Nadajewski and Taylor Garwood.

places.name: Agency & Defiance Exhibit at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Experience never-before-seen works by Toronto-based artist Frantz Brent-Harris inspired by Jamaican Junkanoo. Through these figures, the artist shares the enduring legacy of agency, defiance, resilience, joy, love and cultural expression that sustained enslaved peoples and their descendants, even under inhumane conditions.

places.name: Holiday Artisan Market
places.description: Skip the ordinary and make your holiday shopping a special event! Join us for unique handmade goods from local makers.

places.name: Macbeth
places.address: Crow's Theatre, 345 Carlaw Avenue Toronto, ON M4M 2T1
places.description: One prophecy. One performer. Total collapse. Shakespeare’s most haunting tragedy traces Macbeth’s ruthless climb to power in this solo performance, set against the cutthroat world of the modern tech industry. One prophecy sets the scene for Macbeth’s terrifying unraveling, where every thought, every fear, every choice pushes him beyond the point of no return.

places.name: The Pitch
places.description: Second City’s National Touring Company is hot out of the bullpen, bringing the heat and throwing curveballs as they develop brand new sketches, songs, and improv. Featuring an All-Star cast of comedy powerhouses, this team is sure to hit it out of the park. Batter Up!

places.name: Art Guild of Scarborough's Juried Fall Art Show and Sale
places.address: Centennial Recreation Centre: Scarborough, 1967 Ellesmere Rd
places.description: Featuring over 400 original, juried works of art by member artists, many of whom will be in attendance. Works include watercolour, pastel, oil, acrylic, ink, sculpture and mixed media. The Art Guild of Scarborough is a non-profit organization. Since 1962, it has brought together artists to promote and celebrate the creation of original art. Members range in experience from novice to professional.

places.name: Patterns That Aren't Exhibition
places.address: Cedar Ridge Creative Centre, 225 Confederation Dr
places.description: Step into the intricate world of artist David Currie as he explores how humans are hard-wired to seek out patterns as a means of adapting to their environment, whether connecting imaginary lines to stars or writing algorithms that direct a robot’s movements. But once a pattern is understood, interest tends to fade.

places.name: LEMONS LEMONS LEMONS LEMONS LEMONS
places.address: The Assembly Theatre, 1479 Queen St W
places.description: What would you say if you had only 140 words a day? The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Discover Sam Steiner's play this November. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part romcom, part goofy If-This-Then-What story, and part dystopian exploration of class, gender, language, and communication in relationships.

places.name: Always In Fashion
places.address: Textile Museum of Canada, 55 Centre Ave
places.description: Curated by Amber-Dawn Bear Robe, enjoy an immersive exploration of Indigenous design languages and their transformative impact on the fashion landscape of the lands we call Canada and the United States.

places.name: Queen East Eats Fall Food Tours
places.costNote: Tickets are available for purchase about two weeks before the tour.
places.address: Restaurants/Cafes/Bars in Riverside and Leslieville, 657 Queen St E, Toronto
places.description: Celebrate fall and support small businesses. Get ready to visit six pre-selected local food and drink establishments in Riverside and Leslieville, while learning about the story behind the businesses with your expert guide.

places.name: Retracing Tatreez: Palestinian Thobes through the Twentieth Century
places.costNote: Children 5 and under visit for free.
places.address: Textile Museum of Canada, 55 Centre Ave
places.description: Featuring several examples of Palestinian tatreez (embroidery) from the Textile Museum’s collection, most of which will be exhibited for the first time! Retracing Tatreez highlights what these belongings can tell us about the relationship between Palestinians and their homelands in the twentieth century and beyond.

places.name: TD Encounters: Orison
places.description: Orison (prayer) is a musical collaboration from musician Daniel Áñez and composer James O’Callaghan, connecting science fiction imagery with spirituality and the idea of ‘alien-ness’ in all of its senses: social, cultural, psychological, extra-terrestrial.

places.name: Art for Alzheimer’s
places.address: Todmorden Mills Heritage Site, 67 Pottery Rd
places.description: Art for Alzheimer’s brings together an exceptional collection of original artwork by Canadian illustrator Doug Martin in support of the Alzheimer Society. Spanning 40 years of his career, the exhibition showcases original and commissioned works, offering guests the opportunity to discover, appreciate, and purchase one-of-a-kind artwork while supporting an important cause.

places.name: Storytime At The Park
places.description: Perfect for families and children ages 3 to 9! Enjoy interactive read-alouds of beloved books in English and French, themed activities, nature exploration and a light snack. We can't wait to see you soon at Downsview Park!

places.name: Fall EcoFair Toronto 2026
places.description: A family friendly event that informs and inspires greener choices in our homes and communities. The event is a celebration of all the volunteers, businesses, and organizations working to create a more sustainable Toronto.

places.name: Rebellion Talks: The Rebels' Island Stronghold
places.description: Learn about the violent aftermath of the Rebellion of 1837. The revolutionaries didn't give up easily. Even after Mackenzie's army was crushed at the Battle of Montgomery's Tavern, the rebels kept fighting. They rallied new supporters as they seized control of an island in the Niagara River, declared it to be the independent Republic of Canada, and launched what became known as the Patriot War.

places.name: 2026 Grand Slam: The Inspirational Speaking Finals
places.address: CBC Glenn Gould Studio, 250 Front St W
places.description: The top speakers from this season's competitions return for one night, each delivering a brand new five-minute speech on the 2026 theme, Catalyst. Eight judges from media, business and publishing name the Inspirational Speaker of the Year, with a prize package worth up to $50,000 on the line. Now in its tenth year, Speaker Slam is North America's largest inspirational speaking competition.

places.name: SOL Multicultural Music Festival
places.address: Tribute Communities Recital Hall, 112 Accolade East Building, York University, 83 York Blvd
places.description: Join us at this annual event to celebrate music, art, and dance of the different cultures of Toronto. Expect to see POLKY Art-Folk Band, PLAMEN Slovenian Vocal Group, AVE Choir Toronto, Shamanic Drumming with Peter Arcari, Chinese Opera Performance by Guo Zhiqiang, Korean Traditional Drumming & Fan Dancing by Okja Kim Performance Team, SIRTAKI Dance Workshop, Choral Singing Workshop and ART FAIR in this festival.

places.name: Historic Gingerbread Workshop: Holiday Season at Fort York
places.address: Fort York National Historic Site, 250 Fort York Blvd
places.description: Experience the warmth of the holiday season through a hands-on baking workshop in the historic Officers' Mess Kitchen.

places.name: Cigar Club: 10-Year Anniversary
places.description: Toronto music veterans join the Cigar Club as they hit the stage to celebrate this milestone! Featuring Fortunate Losers and The Young Scones.

places.name: Rudolph Runs Wild
places.address: The Second City - Toronto Mainstage, 110 Harbour St
places.description: Share silliness this holiday season with a jolly extravaganza for kids, parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, and reindeer of all ages! Featuring a fun and festive blend of family-friendly songs and sketches from The Second City’s rich comedy archives, fresh new material written specifically for young audiences, and, of course, the ridiculous improv hijinks The Second City is world famous for.

places.name: Back to Pompeii
places.description: An immersive exhibition that invites guests to step inside ancient Pompeii. Visitors can walk through a Pompeian house and city street, exploring spaces such as a bakery, a thermopolium (an ancient Roman commercial snack bar), a school, a tavern and baths. Guided by an original audio narrative, they can interact with everyday objects while discovering Roman water systems, medicine, food, fragrances and graffiti.

places.name: En Français… Feelings of France by Lisa Litowitz
places.address: Leslie Grove Gallery, 1158 Queen St E
places.description: This new series showcases one year of work from my month in France, including a two week residency and time spent visiting Monet’s gardens at Giverny. This intensive experience allowed me to paint what I saw and felt in the rolling hills, ponds and seductive views of the countryside.

places.name: Diaspora Film Festival
places.description: This festival provides Toronto audiences with an opportunity to experience the cultural mosaic of the present world through the medium of cinema.

places.name: All's Well
places.description: A dark comedy about a cure with wicked fine print. From celebrated Canadian author Mona Awad, writer of the bestselling novels Bunny and We Love You, Bunny, magical realism takes centre stage. After a freak onstage accident ends her promising acting career, Miranda Fitch is left in chronic pain and reduced to directing student Shakespeare productions in a struggling university’s theatre department.

places.name: Old Book and Paper Expo
places.address: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, 6 Sakura Way
places.description: Before the internet there was paper. Vintage paper in the form of rare and unusual books, handwritten letters, vintage postcards, maps, posters, photography, manuscripts and much more. So much paper has been lost over time, burned, trashed, rotted and disintegrated. But some of the best paper has survived and is treasured by people who find joy in collecting vintage paper in all its forms.

places.name: Mayumi Seiler, violin, Min‑Jeong Koh, viola and Daniel Hamin Go, cello
places.address: Mazzoleni Concert Hall, 273 Bloor St W
places.description: Celebrated RCM faculty members and a rising star alumnus unite for an exquisite trio recital of works by Beethoven, Ernő Dohnányi and a new commission by Vancouver-based Stefan Hintersteininger.

places.name: Pages, Pizza and Prosecco: An Evening with The Dutch House
places.address: Miraki Life Space, 35 Golden Avenue, Toronto ON M6R 2J5
places.description: A book club for readers who love good stories and even better company. We are gathering again around Ann Patchett's The Dutch House. We'll keep the plot to ourselves. Just know there's a grand, glass-fronted house, a family, and everything a house holds long after the people have gone. A Pulitzer Prize finalist about memory, family, and the homes that never quite let us go. This isn't your typical book club.

places.name: Music Toronto - Illia Ovcharenko
places.address: Jane Mallett Theatre, St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E
places.description: Having delighted Music Toronto audiences with “one of the best recitals of 2025” (LudwigVanToronto), Ukrainian pianist Illia Ovcharenko returns to Music Toronto with a program shaped by the spirit of fantasy.

places.name: Strings Plus! The Lady with the Hammer
places.address: Trinity- St. Paul's Centre, 427 Bloor St W
places.description: Open the new year with two remarkable soloists and a program built around the drama and drive of timpani. Pianist Élisabeth Pion, Gold Laureate of the 2025 Honens International Piano Competition and a Radio-Canada Breakthrough Artist joins Toronto's own violinist Julia Mirzoev, named one of CBC's Top 30 Classical Musicians Under 30.

places.name: Music Toronto - What Makes It Great with Rob Kapilow and Meagan Milatz
places.address: Jane Mallett Theatre, St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E
places.description: Master communicator Rob Kapilow and brilliant Canadian pianist Meagan Milatz explore Beethoven’s electrifying Appassionata Sonata, revealing how the composer transforms simple musical ideas through bold and imaginative variations.

places.name: WHAT MAKES IT GREAT? - MENDELSSOHN
places.address: Jane Mallett Theatre, St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E
places.description: Featuring Jonathan Crow, violin; Annalee Patipatanakoon, violin; Sharon Wei, viola; Roman Borys, cello; and the Dior String Quartet. In "What Makes It Great?", composer, commentator, and author Rob Kapilow unlocks great music with insight, humour, and live musical examples.

places.name: Ménestrel
places.address: Walter Hall, University of Toronto, 80 Queen's Park
places.description: Celebrate the magic of midwinter with Yuletide: A Ceremony of Midwinter, an enchanting mix of ancient repertoire and traditional folk songs, brought to life through the sounds of lute, recorder and the female voice. Featuring Janelle Lucyk, soprano; Kerry Bursey, lute; and Vincent Lauzer, recorder, this atmospheric performance invites audiences to experience the music, traditions and spirit of the midwinter season.

places.name: More Than a Game: Stories and Legacy of Lacrosse
places.address: Market Gallery, 95 Front St E, Toronto, Second floor
places.description: Join Toronto History Museums’ Chief Curator, Tara Chadwick, in conversation with Lance Winn, Sports Broadcaster and Vice-President of the Arena Lacrosse League, and lacrosse players and supporters as they reflect on the legacy and significance of lacrosse programming. The conversation will highlight the role of lacrosse in supporting youth engagement and building community, connection, and opportunity.

places.name: 2026 Toronto Book Award Winner – By the Lake Book Club
places.address: Assembly Hall, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr
places.description: Presented by: City of Toronto’s Assembly Hall and Toronto Book Awards and Humber Polytechnic’s Faculty of Media, Creative Arts and Design Join the recipient of the 2026 Toronto Book Award for a special discussion celebrating this year's winning book. Recognizing literary excellence and a strong connection to Toronto, the award honours works that contribute to the city's rich cultural and literary landscape.

places.name: Cookie Decorating
places.address: The Elm Tavern, Chelsea Toronto, 22 Elm St, Toronto
places.description: Sprinkles, icing, cookies and Santa, what could be more festive? Bring your little ones for a fun-filled holiday experience where they can decorate their own festive cookies, get creative with all the sweet trimmings and take a selfie with Santa. Join us for an afternoon filled with creativity, laughter and sweet holiday memories. Book now to reserve your spot.

places.name: Breakfast with Santa
places.address: The Elm Tavern, Chelsea Toronto, 22 Elm St, Toronto
places.description: The North Pole is coming to The Elm Tavern! Gather your family and friends for a festive holiday morning featuring a delicious deluxe breakfast buffet filled with sweet and savoury favourites, followed by a special photo with Santa. Join us to make a little holiday magic together. Book now to reserve your spot.

places.name: Music Toronto - Gryphon Trio with James Campbell
places.address: Jane Mallett Theatre, St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E
places.description: In its early years as a Music Toronto ensemble-in-residence, the Gryphon Trio first performed Olivier Messiaen’s visionary "Quartet for the End of Time" with revered Canadian clarinetist James Campbell. Composed in a prisoner-of-war camp during the Second World War, the work stands as one of the 20th century’s most profound musical testaments of faith, transcendence and human resilience.

places.name: Sala-Manca Group: Like a Bird’s Nest
places.description: Enjoy a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group. Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah, a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot.

places.name: Plus One: A Showcase Hosted by ADDO
places.address: Cardinal Carter Academy for the Arts, 36 Greenfield Ave
places.description: As ADDO Company celebrates its fifth year, we're bringing together some of Toronto's incredible dance teams, choreographers, and collectives for PLUS ONE, a celebration of artistry, creativity and the community that connects us. PLUS ONE is a dance showcase that creates space for artists to step outside their individual circles, share their work and experience each other's artistry.

places.name: Christian Heritage Month Celebration
places.address: Toronto City Hall, 100 Queen St West
places.description: Celebrate faith, heritage, and unity in the heart of Toronto, as Christians, families, community leaders, and friends from across the city gather for a meaningful evening honouring Canada’s Christian heritage.

places.name: Remembrance Day at Fort York
places.address: Fort York National Historic Site, 100 Garrison Rd
places.description: Attend one of the City’s most evocative Remembrance Day ceremonies at Fort York National Historic Site. All are encouraged to take part in honouring and remembering the service and sacrifice of all Canadians, from diverse backgrounds and communities, who came together to serve and defend their homes and country. This year also marks the 100th Anniversary of the Royal Canadian Legion.

places.name: The 2026 European Union Film Festival
places.description: A full selection of 28 acclaimed curated films showcasing the breadth of European cinema, taking audiences on a journey from therapy sessions in Sweden and artistic pursuits in Austria to a sci-fi exploration of AI in Romania, encounters with clowns in Estonia, a chaotic reception in Greece and a community’s fight to protect a small Italian island.

places.name: CandyForKids Halloween Candy Drive
places.address: Kumon Centre of Etobicoke, Burnhamthorpe Mall, 666 Burnhamthorpe Rd
places.description: All started by a local student... We collect leftover wrapped candy for kids and families who need it, distributing through community food banks. Be part of this!!

places.name: Imaginary Expedition at Burdock Music Hall
places.address: Burdock Music Hall, 1184 Bloor St W
places.description: Toronto-based duo of Victoria Dobbs and Glyph Greenleaf who combine folk songwriting with early music composition techniques and intimate, unamplified performance practice. The ensemble draws people closer, quietly pushing the limits of what can be achieved with only their alto and baritone voices and a classical guitar.

places.name: Toronto Reel Asian International Film Festival
places.description: Canada’s largest pan-Asian film festival returns for its 30th Anniversary this year. With selected feature films and all shorts available online across Canada, Reel Asian’s milestone edition celebrates three decades of contemporary cinema and work from Asian, Asian diasporic, and Asian Canadian filmmakers and artists.

places.name: Follow The Yellow Brick Road: A Pantomime
places.description: Join us for a re-telling of the classic story of Dorothy, a Kansas girl and her dog, who find themselves lost in a mystical land. On the advice of Gwenda, a Good Witch, and Lance, a similarly misplaced soul, she embarks on a journey to seek help from the Wizard of Oz. Along the way she encounters new friends, talking trees, flying monkeys and an enemy in the Wicked Witch of the West.

places.name: Corpus Christi Parish Craft Fair 2026
places.address: Corpus Christi Parish, 1810 Queen St E
places.description: Gift ideas, kids' activities, bake sale and café. Discover handmade items from local vendors, including sewn, crocheted, and knitted crafts. Honey, preserves and other bee products. Wood crafts, Christmas ornaments, candles, greeting cards, photography, stationery, bath and body products, jewelry and much more!

places.name: Hip-Hop Karaoke
places.description: Flex your lyrical skills on the mic, or kick back and enjoy the show. Hundreds of classic hip-hop anthems to choose from. Don't sleep! Now we're back for another round of classic hip-hop anthems performed by you and your crew! No need to be intimidated — you can roll through, grab a drink and just vibe along.

places.name: Etobicoke Philharmonic Orchestra - Fiesta Sinfónica
places.description: Join us for this evening of rhythm, passion and youthful energy driven by Spanish and Latin American music. Our headliner: Classical guitarist Daniel Ramjattan, performing Rodrigo’s beloved Concierto de Aranjuez, rich with haunting beauty and lyrical elegance.

places.name: WonderPhil's PA Day of Magic
places.description: This interactive show will have the whole family going “ooh” and “ahh” while they laugh out loud. WonderPhil creates the perfect balance of amazement and laughs to keep everyone entertained from beginning to end. After the show, adults and kids alike will be scratching their heads with wonder! His pet parrot Ha-Ha may stop in for a surprise visit too!

places.name: ROM Speaks Kristallnacht "The Night of Broken Glass"
places.description: Iconic Canadian Artists Saul Rubinek and Seana McKenna Perform for one night only. A must-attend night with Saul Rubinek and Seana McKenna, who will perform a dramatic reading from an original theatrical work to commemorate Kristallnacht.

places.name: The possibility of viewing the world differently: Autumn Edition
places.description: A show from curator Deborah Harris, who has gathered artists' works including several drawings by E.J. Gold. Voyage through our nine gallery spaces exploring different themes, mediums, and artists.

places.name: The Happily Ever After Actors
places.description: Meet Henry, Evelyn and Arthur, otherwise known as The Happily Ever Actors! They've made their way to your kingdom to share some of their favourite fairytale stories and you get to be part of the magic! This 30 minute interactive show re-tells the classic tale of Cinderella in a whole new way. They can't wait for you to help bring the story to life!

places.name: Jr. Forest Explorers: Fall Frolic
places.description: Fall is coming to an end and it is time to get outdoors for a forest frolic. Join us for a caregiver and toddler nature program. Connect with the natural world through hands-on outdoor activities and explore seasonal change in this late autumn activity. This program is for children 18 months to three-and-a-half years old. Children up to age four are welcome if they have not started school.

places.name: 14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II
places.costNote: Sign up for the free workshop series on our website.
places.description: The Korean Dance Studies Society brings together artists from Korean, Indigenous, and diverse Canadian artistic traditions through dance, music and cultural exchange. Explore Korean creative dance, K-Pop, African rhythm and movement, beginner tap, Chinese Opera makeup and Korean sangmo dance and janggu drumming.

places.name: Wychwood Library Talk: Managing Invasive Plants Around Your Home
places.description: Join the City of Toronto for a presentation on invasive plants commonly found around homes in Toronto. Learn how to identify these species, understand their impact and effectively manage them. You’ll also get tips on supporting local biodiversity through enhancing native habitats. Perfect for gardeners, homeowners and anyone interested in urban ecology. Drop-in. No registration required.

places.name: Jack and Jill and the Beanstalk
places.description: An Adventure of Giant Proportions! Get ready for a hilarious, larger-than-life adventure as Theatre You Treasure brings the classic fairy tale to life with a delightfully silly twist. Packed with catchy songs, outrageous comedy, colourful characters and plenty of audience participation. A musical pantomime where children are encouraged to cheer for the heroes, boo the villains and help save the day.

places.name: Resonance: A Classical Concert - Leon Lorenz ft. Sinfonia Toronto
places.address: Trinity-St. Paul's United Church and Centre for Faith, Justice and the Arts, 427 Bloor St W
places.description: Join us for a special gala concert celebrating the enduring friendship and diplomatic relations between Germany and Canada through the universal language of music. Resonance: J. S. Bach’s Violin Concerto, Xenakis’ Rebonds, and Corigliano’s The Conjurer, featuring Leon Lorenz and Sinfonia Toronto, followed by an encore of the Recycling Concerto cadenza and Marjan Mozetich’s Songline to Heaven & Dances to Earth.

places.name: Planter by Deanna Armenti
places.description: Experience a temporary public art installation, Planter is an eco-sculpture inspired by the amorphous shapes of old growth forest nursery logs. Planter is one of three sculptures installed across Toronto for a project entitled Ecogenders. These three installations collaborate with their respective ecosystems to decay and regrow into the land.

places.name: Humber Summit Library Tree Tour
places.description: The Humber Summit Library and its neighbourhood is home to a variety of trees. Join the City to explore the natural world on a local neighbourhood tour. Learn how to recognize different species, and fun facts about their cultural and ecological importance. Free program. Children under 12 must be accompanied by a parent/caregiver. Registration is required.

places.name: Jack and Jill and the Beanstalk - January 2027
places.description: An Adventure of Giant Proportions! Get ready for a hilarious, larger-than-life adventure as Theatre You Treasure brings the classic fairy tale to life with a delightfully silly twist. Packed with catchy songs, outrageous comedy, colourful characters and plenty of audience participation. A musical pantomime where children are encouraged to cheer for the heroes, boo the villains and help save the day.

places.name: Holiday Fair in Sankofa Square
places.address: Sankofa Square, 1 Dundas St E, Toronto
places.description: Celebrate the Holiday season right in the heart of downtown Toronto! Enjoy twinkling lights, a Holiday Market featuring local artisans, delicious treats and cozy firepits with mulled wine and spiked hot chocolate. Visit Santa for a photo and explore fun holiday photo opportunities. Take a moment to share the spirit of giving at The Giving Tree. Best of all, this holiday celebration is in support of Epilepsy Toronto!

places.name: Comedy Railroad: Next Generation – Live Comedy Album Recording
places.address: Olde Stone Cottage Pub, 3750 Kingston Rd
places.description: Scarborough’s Got Jokes is teaming up with Comedy Records to bring a special live comedy album recording to one of Scarborough’s most historic venues. Comedy Railroad, founded by Daniel Woodrow and Rodney Ramsey, is recognized as Canada's first all-Black comedy tour. Now, Comedy Railroad: Next Generation continues that legacy, showcasing a new wave of talented Black Canadian comedians.

places.name: Bravissimo! New Year's at the Opera
places.description: This New Year's Eve, the romance, drama, and grandeur of opera's greatest hits returns for a one-of-a-kind concert event. Backed by the power of the Canadian Opera Company Orchestra, four international stars perform genre-defining selections from the greatest operas ever written during this glamourous experience. End your year on a high note!

places.name: VERSUS
places.address: The Theatre Centre, 1115 Queen St W
places.description: From award-winning Canadian artistic collaborators Adam Lazarus, Guillermo Verdecchia, and Ann-Marie Kerr comes Versus, a laugh-out-loud experience that can only happen in the theatre. Cake included. It is Gerald Bloom’s birthday and he doesn’t want to go to his party - everything feels like a fight.

places.name: Rebellion Talks: Riots & the Rebel Mayor
places.description: Learn about the riots that shook Toronto to its core in the years before and after the Rebellion of 1837 in the rebel mayor’s former home, which is now Mackenzie House Museum. Political violence was a common occurrence in Toronto; rival factions battled in our streets.

places.name: Light in the Darkness - Find the Beauty: The Upper Canada Choristers and Cantemos in concert
places.costNote: Children 16 and under free when accompanied by an adult.
places.description: Light up the night with a holiday concert! Featuring an engaging mix of Christmas music from over the centuries, in English and Spanish, along with songs for Chanukah, Kwanzaa and more. Latin ensemble Cantemos serves up songs from South America. Hye Won (Cecilia) Lee is pianist, with Nora Dunn as M.C.

places.name: Shab-e She’r Poetry Fourteenth Anniversary
places.description: Canada’s most diverse and brave poetry reading and open mic series. Featured poets include Mary Simmerling and Subrata Kumar Das. Hosted by Bänoo Zan. Mary Simmerling is a poet, philosopher, and inter-arts artist whose poem “What I Was Wearing” inspired the internationally recognized What Were You Wearing? survivor art installations.

places.name: Hotel X Toronto Announces “A Merry & Mischievous Breakfast With Santa” for the 2026 Holiday Season
places.address: Hotel X Toronto, 111 Princes’ Blvd., Toronto
places.description: Celebrate the magic of the season with a playful twist! Families are invited to enjoy a festive holiday experience featuring story time and photos with Santa. You can also expect appearances from a mischievous green holiday guest, festive music and magic from DJ Buck and his rabbit companion Snowball, airbrush tattoos and a variety of seasonal activities.

places.name: Jr. Forest Explorers: Celebration of Light and Sunshine
places.description: Join us for a caregiver and toddler nature program. Connect with the natural world through hands-on outdoor activities.

places.name: Gather for Storytelling at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Join this storytelling circle with Maria Ordóñez as she shares stories from around the world. This gathering celebrates the oral storytelling tradition and welcomes people of all ages and abilities. The theme for October is "Autumn Gatherings: Myths, Legends, and Tales." Attendees are encouraged to choose a folktale and tell it from their own perspective.

places.name: Comfy Cozy Concert
places.description: In the space between Halloween and the winter holidays, when you're not sure if it's autumn or winter, come in from the cold, listen to some music, do some crafts, get your tarot cards read, have a drink and enjoy! Put on your comfiest knit sweater and wool socks and join us for an indie concert featuring 4 up-and-coming artists based in and around Toronto.

places.name: Play Mobile at Jimmie Simpson Park
places.address: Jimmie Simpson Park, 872 Queen St E
places.description: Play Mobile is a free touring sports program for all ages and skill levels, no registration or reservations are required to participate. The new soccer Play Mobile is dedicated to the world’s most popular game. All ages are invited to learn and celebrate soccer in a fun, supportive environment with no experience required.

places.name: Miracle on Bloor - Toronto’s Original Christmas Bar
places.address: Miracle on Bloor, 875 Bloor St. West
places.description: The ultimate Christmas playground! Expect floor-to-ceiling décor, extravagant holiday-themed cocktails, a delicious snack menu from Fat Rice, Drumming Santa appearances, live DJ sets on Fridays, Drag Brunch events every Saturday, late night happy hour promos and tons of festive photo moments.

places.name: Rummage Sale
places.description: Looking to clear out your closets, garage, or kitchen cabinets? We need your gently used treasures to make this year's charity donation a massive success! Drop off your items at the church fellowship hall and let us do the rest.

places.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony at East York Civic Centre
places.address: East York Civic Centre, Memorial Gardens, 850 Coxwell Ave
places.description: Join the City of Toronto in honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of Canada’s fallen heroes. Wear a poppy and come together for a moment of collective reflection and gratitude in the Memorial Gardens in front of East York Civic Centre. This year marks the centennial of the Royal Canadian Legion. The East York Civic Centre ceremony is one of several Remembrance Day ceremonies taking place across the city.

places.name: The Magic is Waiting: Holiday Season at Todmorden Mills
places.address: Todmorden Mills Heritage Site, 67 Pottery Rd
places.description: Experience how the Valley lights up for the season. Follow the glow of seasonal lights and explore traditions of illumination from different cultures and time periods. Enjoy hands-on seasonal crafts in the Brewery Building, sip a warm beverage and visit the festively decorated historic houses of Todmorden as part of a free tour. Tours at 11:30 a.m., 1 p.m. and 2:30 p.m.

places.name: Holiday Season Sale at Toronto History Museums
places.description: Find unique gifts inspired by Toronto's history and save this holiday season. Shop museum-inspired gifts, books, home décor, toys, holiday treasures, and locally crafted items at Toronto History Museums gift shops and online store. Whether you're searching for a meaningful gift or a special keepsake, our holiday sales are the perfect opportunity to save.

places.name: Remembrance Day at the Swansea Town Hall
places.description: The Swansea Town Hall and the Swansea Branch of the Royal Canadian Legion commemorate the men of Swansea who gave their lives in WWI and for whom the Swansea Memorial Library was created. We also honour all those who served in wars, peace keeping missions and sacrificed themselves for our Country. Everyone is welcome.

places.name: Freely - A Mixed Media Cabaret
places.address: Super Wonder Gallery, 1162 Bloor St W
places.description: Join us for a variety of fresh, performative works by Toronto artists from the theatre, music and dance communities. This mixed media variety show offers artists and audiences an opportunity to meet mid-genesis, with works that are both in “testing phase” and sneak-peak excerpts of those ready for full productions.

places.name: The Distillery Winter Village
places.address: The Distillery Historic District, 55 Mill Street Toronto
places.description: Turning into a European-inspired Christmas market, with thousands of lights, dozens of seasonal food and drink vendors, and festive shopping across thirteen acres of Victorian brickwork. Known as the city's most atmospheric holiday outing, especially for food lovers, with festive treats and warm drinks around every cobblestone corner.

places.name: An Evening of Fashion History with Linda V. Carter at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Join actress, media personality and producer Linda V. Carter for an evening exploring Canadian fashion and history. Linda shares personal stories connecting her family history with fashion design, discussing the experiences of Black communities in Toronto and Canada in the 1930s and her own experiences as one of Canada's first Black models.

places.name: Ecosystem Connects: AI and Beyond - Kick-off to the TPL AI Summit
places.description: ​Kick off the Toronto Public Library AI Summit with a half-day forum presented by the City of Toronto’s Office of Technology and Innovation Sectors. ​Ecosystem Connects: AI and Beyond brings together leaders from government, industry, academia, and the startup community to explore how Toronto can strengthen its position as a global leader in AI and emerging technologies, including quantum computing.

places.name: Beaded Poppy Workshop with Marissa Magneson at Fort York
places.address: Fort York National Historic Site, 250 Fort York Blvd
places.description: Make your own beautiful beaded poppy patch to honour Indigenous Veterans Day and the service, sacrifice and contributions of First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples to Canada’s military history. Led by Marissa Magneson, a Cree-Métis artist, photographer, educator and workshop facilitator, you can discover the art of flat stitch beadwork with this workshop designed specifically for beginner and intermediate beaders.

places.name: The Sororum Presents: A Step Through Time
places.address: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W
places.description: Join us for a memorable day of history, artistry, discovery and meaningful connection in Toronto's charming Yorkville neighbourhood. Our journey begins at the iconic Bata Shoe Museum with a private guided tour exploring fascinating stories of Roman history and the artistry of beaded footwear across cultures. We'll then discover traditional leatherworking techniques and create our own keepsake.

places.name: The Professionals Comedy Show - Toronto's Best Stand-Up Comedy
places.description: Canada's top stand-up comics unite to deliver an evening of hilarity! Acts have been featured on: Just For Laughs, CBC, Sirius XM and more! When amateur comedy isn't doing the job, it's time to call The Professionals. A line-up of Canada's most acclaimed comics come together to leave you in stitches! Located in a legendary performance space that is perfect for an intimate stand-up comedy show.

places.name: THE KING’S GRIEF - The Happenstancers
places.address: Redeemer Lutheran Church, 1691 Bloor St W
places.description: The wolves cry, an end foretold. Presenting Judith Weir’s micro-opera King Harald’s Saga, punctuating Weir's tragic narrative with the music of Thomas Adès, Oliver Knussen, Thierry Tidrow, Mary Dering, John Dowland. Casting the works as incidental music within a larger drama.

places.name: Pet Photos with Santa
places.address: The Elm Tavern, Chelsea Toronto, 22 Elm St, Toronto
places.description: The holidays are for everyone, including our furry family members! Bring your beloved pet to The Elm Tavern for a festive photo with Santa and create a special holiday memory to cherish. The package includes a photo with Santa and a special holiday treat for your pet. Book now to reserve your spot.

places.name: A Day of Music - Music Creators Day 2026
places.address: Cloverdale Common, Cloverdale Mall, 250 The East Mall
places.description: Join us for a day of live music, featuring 25 local music creators from across Etobicoke and West Toronto. Catch live sets, hear directly from artists about how they make their music and join in on family-friendly music activities.

places.name: The T.O. You Don’t Know
places.address: Museum of Toronto, 401 Richmond St W LL01
places.description: Uncover hidden stories Toronto has long overlooked. Explore the history of over 70 historic sites, forgotten events, fascinating local narratives and unique objects. It surfaces the ignored, the hyperlocal and the quietly radical, reinforcing that history is not fixed, but layered and still unfolding.

places.name: Out of Line: 150 Years of Supporting Creative Defiance at OCAD U
places.description: The Student Galleries mark OCAD University’s 150th anniversary with a pointed declaration of purpose by positioning the institution not merely as a site of technical training or aesthetic refinement, but rather as a long-standing incubator of creative disruption. The exhibition gathers notable alumni and long-time faculty whose practices embody this refusal.

places.name: "Newn" Year Celebration: Holiday Season at Gibson House
places.description: Enjoy a free festive museum visit filled with holiday charm. Drop by and experience a historic kitchen demonstration, create your own Gibson House-inspired paper ornament and enjoy seasonal holiday music throughout the museum. Free.

places.name: What Is the Role of Empathy in Democracy?
places.costNote: Or register to join the livestream for free.
places.address: Globe and Mail Centre 17th Floor, 351 King St E
places.description: Rarely do leaders gather to examine one question from so many perspectives. Join us at our 30th Anniversary Symposium.

places.name: Buckthorn Wreath-Making
places.description: Did you know that buckthorn is one of the most invasive shrubs in Ontario? Help us transform these destructive plants into beautiful fall decorations. You’ll have the opportunity to create a stunning wreath using pre-cut buckthorn and other natural materials. This festive and eco-friendly activity is perfect for getting into the fall spirit!

places.name: Croissant Class in Toronto
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: A beginner friendly class where you’ll learn how to layer butter, roll laminated dough and shape croissants. Take home about a dozen or more unbaked croissants to bake at home, plus the recipe emailed before class. All ingredients, equipment and transport boxes are provided. Please note that the class involves a lot of rolling and layering and the studio may be upstairs with stair-only access.

places.name: Holiday Open House 2026
places.description: Start and finish your shopping at 401 Richmond this festive season with 18 galleries, 2 shops, a licensed café and an underground cinema. Find artwork, books, cards, clothing, jewelry, objects, toys and much more.

places.name: Cultural Hotspot In-Person Funding Info Session: KGO
places.address: Morningside Branch, Toronto Public Library, 4279 Lawrence Ave E
places.description: The City of Toronto's Cultural Hotspot program is offering funding for arts, culture and community projects that celebrate the people, places and stories of Kingston-Galloway/Orton Park (KGO). From June to October 2027, Cultural Hotspot will shine a spotlight on the KGO community through workshops, events and community activities.

places.name: A Legacy in Motion: The National Ballet of Canada at 75
places.address: Toronto Reference Library, TD Gallery, 789 Yonge St
places.description: Explore 75 years of The National Ballet of Canada through archival content from Toronto Public Library Special Collections and The National Ballet of Canada Archives. Featuring costume designs, photography, show worn costumes and more!

places.name: Scarborough’s Delicious Secrets: Woks, Broths, and the Suburban Chinatown
places.address: Lang Chai Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine, 3280 Midland Ave unit 27&28
places.description: Agincourt, also lovingly known as ‘Asiancourt’, is the beating heart of East Asian dining in Toronto, where unassuming strip plazas hide some of the most dynamic regional cooking in North America.

places.name: Workshop: Make Moisturizing Cream at Karma Co-op
places.address: Karma Co-op Grocery Store, 739 Palmerston Ave Toronto, Ontario M6G 2R3
places.description: Dread the feeling of dry, itchy skin? The obnoxious fragrances and unreadable ingredients of drugstore moisturizing lotions? Want to moisturize and nourish your skin without feeling like you've been dunked in a tank of grease? You will learn how to make a basic white lotion from scratch. We will turn that lotion into a Simply Shea Cream.

places.name: Between Suns Concept Launch: Chapter One
places.description: Between Suns is a new Black-led Toronto cultural experience combining Oldowan Co.’s three-act FW26 runway presentation with six original songs performed live, a curated Black-owned marketplace and the introduction of a larger citywide festival vision for 2027.

places.name: Northern Noir Market
places.description: You are invited to come in out of the cold and join us. Showcasing 35 plus artists, artisans and authors celebrating all aspects of the season, especially those that are dark, macabre and spooky. Our market is majority kid friendly. Our gorgeous venue is close to parking and transit, is fully accessible and has an ATM on site. The bar will be open for customers to enjoy a beverage while they shop.

places.name: Fire Building with Kory Snache
places.description: Kory Snache is a cultural land-based educator that works for Wasauksing First Nation. He is from Rama First Nation and has been a traditional harvester for the majority of his life. Join us as we learn about Anishnaabeg general understanding of fire and how to create a fire in all seasons. Participants will get to go outside and gather material and try various ways in which to start a fire.

places.name: Rough Draft

places.description: Try something new, get moving and connect through sport, Play Mobile is a free touring sports program for all ages and skill levels. With a variety of sports equipment on board, vibrant vans tour neighbourhoods, transforming parks and outdoor spaces into pop-up sport hubs, bringing energy and excitement directly to communities around the city.

places.name: The Devin Cuddy Band
places.description: A JUNO-nominated, Toronto-based roots country band led by pianist and singer-songwriter Devin Cuddy, son of Blue Rodeo’s Jim Cuddy. They are recognized for their unique blend of New Orleans blues and country. Their April 2026 album Livin’ Hard Ain’t Easy, is a return to their original sound. It’s a country record, made for and about Canadians.

places.name: Halls of Joy
places.address: Humber Valley United Church, 76 Anglesey Blvd. Etobicoke ON M9A 3C1, 76 Anglesey Blvd
places.description: Join us for the opening concert of our 60th anniversary season! This festive celebration of Christmas features Bach’s Cantata no.140, Sleepers Awake, Galuppi’s shining Magnificat in G and Buxtehude’s Das neugeborne Kindelein (The Newborn Child). Accompanied by an authentic Baroque orchestra, the music of the season is brought to life with the colours, textures and performance practices of the era.

places.name: Play Mobile at Riverdale Park E
places.address: Riverdale Park E, 550 Broadview Ave, Toronto
places.description: Play Mobile is a free touring sports program for all ages and skill levels, no registration or reservations are required to participate. The new soccer Play Mobile is dedicated to the world’s most popular game. All ages are invited to learn and celebrate soccer in a fun, supportive environment with no experience required.

places.name: Play Mobile at Coronation Park
places.description: Try something new, get moving and connect through sport, Play Mobile is a free touring sports program for all ages and skill levels. With a variety of sports equipment on board, vibrant vans tour neighbourhoods, transforming parks and outdoor spaces into pop-up sport hubs, bringing energy and excitement directly to communities around the city.

places.name: Play Mobile at Giltspur Park
places.address: Giltspur Park, 85 Magellan Dr, North York
places.description: Try something new, get moving and connect through sport, Play Mobile is a free touring sports program for all ages and skill levels. With a variety of sports equipment on board, vibrant vans tour neighbourhoods, transforming parks and outdoor spaces into pop-up sport hubs, bringing energy and excitement directly to communities around the city.

places.name: Art of Henna: Holiday Season at Scarborough Museum
places.description: Enjoy a hands-on henna workshop with artist Elavarasi from Lotus Henna Toronto. Adorn your hands with traditional designs that celebrate cultural expression and intergenerational artistry. Learn about the history, symbolism and techniques of henna while reflecting on its role in ceremonies and celebrations.

places.name: (Sold Out) Rebellion Talks: Booze, Taverns & Rowdy Rebels
places.description: Learn the role Toronto's raucous taverns played in the political tensions leading up to the Rebellion of 1837. In the middle of the 1800s, taverns played a central role in political life. Montgomery’s Inn served as a watering hole during those tense years, making it the perfect place to discuss Toronto’s tavern history and how these places helped set the stage for Mackenzie’s attempted revolution.

places.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony at Etobicoke Civic Centre
places.address: Etobicoke Civic Centre Cenotaph, 399 The West Mall
places.description: Join the City of Toronto in honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of Canada’s fallen heroes. Wear a poppy and come together for a moment of collective reflection and gratitude in front of the cenotaph at Etobicoke Civic Centre. This year marks the centennial of the Royal Canadian Legion. The Etobicoke Civic Centre ceremony is one of several Remembrance Day ceremonies taking place across the city.

places.name: The Sound of Music Sing Along at TIFF Lightbox
places.description: TIFF Lightbox is alive with the sound of music! Impress everyone with your best Julie Andrews impersonation and frolic among the cinema aisles at this sing-along edition of The Sound of Music, hosted by comedian Martha Chaves, a.k.a. Sister Martha. Dress up in your lederhosen/dirndl, don your own habit or, if you have neither, a DIY costume from old curtains will do just fine!

places.name: Comedy At The Campbells: The Naughty List
places.address: Campbell House Museum, 160 Queen St W
places.description: A fabulous festive fundraiser for Campbell House Museum! Toronto's most fabulous historic house invites you to attend an amazing intimate evening of entertainment, with a dream lineup of Canada's funniest comedians. Join us for cocktails and camaraderie as Toronto's top comics serve up a show that's sure to tickle your festive funnybone! Be aware, this toast to the season will be extra cheeky!

places.name: Christmas Book Sale
places.costNote: $2 cash admission on the first day only.
places.address: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 789 Yonge St
places.description: Holidays are arriving early at the Reference Library! Perfect for the gift-giving season, find deep discounts on books, CDs, DVDs and other pre-loved items at our annual Christmas Sale. Fiction, nonfiction, art books, cookbooks, children and youth books — there’s something for everyone. As always, all proceeds will be donated in support of Toronto Public Library programs. Please bring your own bags.

places.name: JellyCat Amuseables Heart Cake Class
places.costNote: per person (plus applicable taxes and fees at checkout)
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: This 2-hour class is beginner-friendly and inspired by the JellyCat Amuseables collection. Guests learn how to fill and stack a heart-shaped cake, apply buttercream, create texture and sculpt fondant details to give their cake personality. Participants take home a fully decorated vanilla cake and receive vanilla cake, American buttercream and Swiss meringue buttercream recipes before class.

places.name: Scarborough Community Multicultural Festival - Winterfest
places.description: Scarborough’s signature two‑day winter celebration, transforming Albert Campbell Square at the Scarborough Civic Centre into a vibrant, family‑friendly festival filled with cultural pride, seasonal magic, and community spirit. The event brings together residents, visitors, performers and vendors for an immersive holiday experience that highlights the diversity and creativity of Toronto’s east end.

places.name: Artist Walk and Talk with Deanna Armenti
places.address: Meet at Colborne Lodge (High Park) 11 Colborne Lodge Dr.
places.description: Hear firsthand from the artist about the temporary public artwork, Planter, in High Park. Planter is an eco-sculpture inspired by the amorphous shapes of old growth forest nursery logs. The work is made of ethically sourced wood from urban trees around Toronto at the end of their life cycle. The tour begins at Colborne Lodge and then goes down to the sculpture.

places.name: Evening Tour & Craft: Holiday Season at Spadina Museum
places.description: Experience the magic of the season with an evening guided tour. See the lavish 55-room mansion fully decorated for Christmas, just as it was in the 1920s. Sample festive punch and treats. In this rare opportunity to enjoy the house by night, an expert guide shares holiday traditions of the Austin family and the servants who lived and worked in the grand house.

places.name: Riverside Antler Breakfast - Annual Fundraiser
places.address: Ralph Thornton Community Centre, 765 Queen St E
places.description: Now in its 15th year, this annual festive community fundraiser and celebration will be in support of Fontbonne Ministries’ Food Program at Mustard Seed, serving over 25,000 meals to people in need annually, and Ralph Thornton Community Centre programming for low income seniors and youth.

places.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony at Scarborough War Memorial
places.description: Join the City of Toronto in honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of Canada’s fallen heroes. Wear a poppy and come together for a moment of collective reflection and gratitude in front of Scarborough War Memorial. The Scarborough War Memorial ceremony is one of several Remembrance Day ceremonies taking place across the city.

places.name: Gingerbread Cookie Class
places.costNote: (plus applicable taxes and fees at checkout)
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: A beginner-friendly class where guests learn to roll, cut, bake, and decorate gingerbread cookies using royal icing. All ingredients, equipment, and transport boxes are provided, and guests take home approximately 12 decorated cookies, new decorating skills and recipes emailed after class. Designs are guided by the instructor, and an apron is available as an optional add-on.

places.name: Holiday Season Market at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Celebrate the season at this special once-a-year market, featuring a curated selection of local craft and artisanal vendors. Browse unique handmade goods and treat yourself to delicious locally made products. Enjoy the festive atmosphere, support local makers and find something special for everyone on your holiday list.

places.name: The Other Reindeer, A Choral Panto Show, Singing Out’s Holiday concert
places.address: Chrysalis Theatre (TMU - The Creative School Chrysalis), 43 Gerrard St E, Toronto
places.description: Toronto’s Largest 2SLGBTQQIA+ choir presents a one-of-a-kind choral panto show! When the North Pole’s most famous flyer falls from the sky, three unlikely contenders compete to lead the sleigh. Bringing together the joy of choir music and the magic of holiday panto, this show will dazzle and delight. Let the Reindeer Games Begin!

places.name: Tiramisu Masterclass
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: The 1.5-hour Tiramisu Masterclass teaches guests how to make this classic Italian dessert, including preparing silky sabayon, selecting quality ingredients, making ladyfinger biscuits, layering, assembling and garnishing tiramisu. Participants will create and take home a complete tiramisu while learning helpful techniques, troubleshooting tips, and variations they can recreate at home.

places.name: Merry Loo-Crew: Decking the Stalls
places.address: Trinity Bellwoods Park, 790 Queen St W
places.description: Who says holiday cheer can’t happen in the loo? Bringing a surprise carolling activation to public bathrooms across Toronto, and it’s anything but ordinary. Meet a troupe of festive carollers performing cheeky twists on holiday classics in one of the most overlooked rooms throughout the city.

places.name: Dr. Draw Holiday Extravaganza 2026
places.description: Canadian electric violin pioneer Dr. Draw and his band The Strange Parade return for their annual holiday show, featuring Canadian Beatbox Champion Scott Jackson and a few other surprise guests. This year’s show will feature old school Dr. Draw classics, new unreleased tracks and a brand new holiday program created just for the occasion. A holiday show for all ages!

places.name: Remembering GECO Girls of Scarborough at Scarborough Museum
places.description: Join author and local historian Barbara Dickson for a presentation on Bomb Girls: Trading Aprons for Ammo and explore the stories of Scarborough's own GECO Girls. View a pop-up panel highlighting the women who worked at the GECO munitions factory, Canada's largest fuse-filling munitions factory during the Second World War, and learn about their contributions and sacrifices to the war effort.

places.name: Carol Sing-Along with the Music Studio at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Join the Music Studio students for this free annual holiday sing-along. Enjoy your favourite festive tunes and seasonal classics, sharing in the holiday spirit with family and friends. This family-friendly event is sure to delight all ages.

places.name: Winter Tea at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Come for a winter tea to enjoy a plate of seasonal sweets and bottomless tea. Two seating times are available. Tickets are non-refundable. Sweets contain gluten, dairy, eggs and may contain traces of nuts.

places.name: Story Planet: Book Launch
places.address: Morningside Branch, Toronto Public Library, 4279 Lawrence Ave E
places.description: Celebrate the launch of Stories We Couldn't Keep to Ourselves, a picture book anthology written and illustrated by 16 youth authors from Scarborough’s Kingston-Galloway/Orton Park (KGO) neighbourhood. Developed during skill building workshops facilitated by professional authors and illustrators, this project features original stories inspired by the people and places within the KGO community.

places.name: Good Morning Science!
places.address: Medical Sciences Building, University of Toronto St. George Campus, 1 King's College Crcl
places.description: Enjoy a day of fun, hands-on STEM activities for kids, a robotics workshop and a tasty lunch. All proceeds will support Pueblo Science’s outreach programs that promote science literacy worldwide.

places.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony at Old City Hall
places.address: Old City Hall Cenotaph, 60 Queen St W
places.description: Join the City of Toronto in honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of Canada’s fallen heroes. Wear a poppy and come together for a moment of collective reflection and gratitude in front of Old City Hall. This year marks the centennial of the Royal Canadian Legion. The Old City Hall ceremony is one of several Remembrance Day ceremonies taking place across the city.

places.name: At the Table - Grand Social
places.address: St. Regis Toronto, St. Regis Ballroom, 325 Bay St.
places.description: Join us for a Grand Social featuring exceptional producers from France and Germany. Meet the winemakers behind the wines and taste openly a selection of their finest cuvées, while enjoying unlimited delicious food offerings from some of Toronto’s best restaurants, such as Barberian's Steak House, FAV Craft Kitchen, No Vacancy and Sushi Yūgen.

places.name: Off Peak Perks - Apple Pie Class
places.address: Le Dolci Culinary School, 12 Sousa Mendes St
places.description: This class is perfect for beginners, it teaches guests how to make flaky pie dough, prepare apple filling, assemble a pie and decorate it with a lattice top or dough cutouts. Each guest takes home a 9-inch unbaked apple pie to bake at home or freeze for later, along with pastry dough and apple filling recipes emailed before class. All ingredients and equipment are provided.

places.name: Skate Lending Library at Dufferin Grove Park
places.address: Dufferin Grove Park, 875 Dufferin St, Toronto
places.description: Don't have skates but want to take a spin around the ice? Enjoy the use of free skates, helmets and skate aides today.

places.name: Meeting of the Minds: A Toronto Hip Hop Town hall
places.description: In celebration of Hip-Hop History Month, this event brings artists, educators, students and community members together to celebrate the evolution of Toronto's Hip-Hop scene and build on its momentum — sharing hard-won lessons, tackling shared challenges and shaping solutions together in a town hall format for the road ahead.

places.name: Holiday Season Carols in the Tavern at Montgomery's Inn
places.description: Celebrate the season with an evening of traditional carols, folk music, historic food and community in the nearly 200-year-old tavern. Gather with friends and family, sing along to some festive favourites, and experience the warmth of the holiday season. Snacks and drinks are available for purchase. This event is intended for adults.

places.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony at York Cemetery, North York
places.description: Join the City of Toronto in honouring the courage, sacrifice and service of Canada’s fallen heroes. Wear a poppy and come together for a moment of collective reflection and gratitude at the cenotaph in York Cemetery. This year marks the centennial of the Royal Canadian Legion. The North York Cenotaph ceremony is one of several Remembrance Day ceremonies taking place across the city.

places.name: Pollinator-Friendly Seed Saving Workshop
places.description: Come and learn about some pollinator-friendly plants you can bring to your garden, along with how to collect and save the seeds they produce each year. Share the seeds with friends, family and neighbours to create even more pollinator habitat and spread the joy of native plant gardening around! This workshop will have both an indoor and outdoor component.

places.name: Family Solstice: Holiday Season at Colborne Lodge
places.address: Colborne Lodge, 11 Colborne Lodge Dr, Toronto
places.description: Share in winter traditions from around the world from past and present inside the cozy, festive High Park cottage. Take a short tour before gathering around the fireplace for a live reading of a family-friendly Christmas ghost story. Enjoy a warm seasonal beverage and sweet treats to complete your experience.

places.name: Leslieville's 20th Annual Wanderlust
places.address: Queen Street East (Empire Ave to Vacouver Ave)
places.description: Explore local shops, galleries and eateries along Queen Street E. Our BIA businesses will be hosting special promotions, in-store activations and seasonal treats all day long! Featuring a prize wheel, live DJ, photobooth and hot cider. At Leslie Grove Park experience Santa’s village, trackless train rides, fire pits and marshmallows and a tree lighting ceremony at sunset.

places.name: LAT Wellbeing Walks: River Resonances by Treva Legassie
places.description: Join LAT for the final Wellbeing Walk of Autumn. The Wellbeing Walks series invites an artist every season to create an engaging experience that explores the interconnectedness of the wellbeing of self with the wellbeing of the natural world. ​River Resonances by Treva Legassie is a soundwalk that will invite participants to collectively and individually attune to the acoustic environment of Biidaasige Park.

places.name: Lasting Letters: An Evening with Frish Brandt & Dr. Samir Sinha
places.description: "Letter midwife" Frish Brandt joins geriatrician Dr. Samir Sinha for a conversation presented in conjunction with Richard Avedon Immortal. Brandt was Richard Avedon’s longtime art dealer at San Francisco’s Fraenkel Gallery before becoming a “letter midwife.” She joins Dr.

places.name: Lynn Miles
places.description: Lynn Miles has the kind of voice that, when you first hear it, you must find out who she is. She’s been blessed with a drop-dead beautiful honey smooth voice that’s impossible to ignore. It rides along the ebb and flow of a gifted sense of melody. She’s the kind of lyricist who renders whatever heartache you feel into something both beautiful and aching, she is also extremely funny.

places.name: 22 Anniversary Party of CHHA 1610 AM
places.description: La Voz de la Comunidad! Join us for an unforgettable night of live music, dancing and community spirit! Celebrate CHHA ’s 22nd anniversary, honoring with artists! For 22 years, CHHA 1610 AM, Canada’s first Spanish radio station with a community ethnic CRTC license, has brought people together through music, stories and programming that reflect the voices of our Spanish-speaking community.

places.name: BBNC Winter Concert 2026
places.description: Join us for a wonderful evening of live music, singing, dancing and community spirit! Our Winter Concert will feature performances by the BBCC Band, BBNC Glee Club and BBNC Dancers. Guests can enjoy an entertaining evening with refreshments, a 50/50 raffle and the opportunity to connect with friends and neighbours. Proceeds from the evening will support BBNC's Share365 Program.

places.name: Kuchocki Sings DiNovi - But Only For You
places.description: Juliann Kuchocki releases a landmark collaboration with jazz legend Gene Dinovi featuring new music by Peggy Lee Internationally acclaimed vocalist, producer and artistic director Juliann Kuchocki has announced the worldwide release of her newest recording.

places.name: Cicada Woods Album Release with guests Medusa Quarte
places.description: A Canadian all-women tango-fusion string quartet. Pushing the sonic limits of violin, viola, cello and double bass, the ensemble uses percussive effects, scratches, siren wails and driving rhythms to create an electrifying sound that bridges Argentine tango, classical tradition and fearless contemporary experimentation.

places.name: Let’s Talk Burnout, Leadership Responsibility
places.description: Bringing artists and industry leaders together for an evening exploring the role of leadership in creating healthier, more supportive music-industry workplaces. Moderated by Catherine Harrison, the conversation will explore how venue owners, managers, artists and other industry leaders can help build cultures where people feel supported, respected and psychologically safe.

places.name: Holiday Magic
places.address: Village of Yorkville Park, 115 Cumberland St
places.description: Kick off the holiday season in the heart of Yorkville at the official lighting ceremony. The evening features a live concert by Canadian jazz icon Molly Johnson, with special guests the Rosedale Day School Choir. Hosted by television personality Melissa Grelo. Join the community for an evening of music, festive lights and seasonal cheer as the neighbourhood’s holiday lights are switched on.

places.name: Symposium: A Black History of Photography
places.address: School of Image Arts, 122 Bond St
places.description: Join us for a day of talks by international scholars and artists examining photography through the lens of Black history and experience. From the invention of photography, Black populations across the globe have been at the forefront of the technology’s innovation and social use.

places.name: Heroes on the Air
places.description: In the time before the internet and before television, friends and families gathered to watch the glowing light of the radio and to listen to their weekly stories. This immersive theatre experience transports audiences behind the glowing light, as they enter the world of a live 1940’s radio studio broadcast! Let us take you back to the golden age of radio.

places.name: The Stories We Keep: A Writing and Storytelling Workshop
places.address: Toronto Public Library - Wychwood Branch, 1431 Bathurst St
places.description: Bring an object that matters to you and spend an afternoon exploring the memories, people, places, and moments held within the objects we keep through writing, reflection, and conversation. Led by a former archaeologist, you'll use guided prompts and archaeology-inspired approaches to uncover the stories and meaning behind one meaningful object from home.

places.name: 33 ANNUAL - RIVERDALE SHARE HOLIDAY CONCERT 2026
places.description: For 33 years, the Riverdale Share Concert has been bringing holiday magic to the stage while making a meaningful difference in our community. This spectacular annual musical extravaganza combines the joy of the season with the spirit of giving, raising much-needed funds and collecting food for local charities.

places.name: Beau Dixon & Friends
places.description: Beau Dixon is an award winning musician, singer, songwriter, music director, actor and playwright. He will be bringing his all star band to tear the roof off the venue with his energetic blend of original soul, r&b, reggae, funk and rock music. Along with throwing in some classic hits by Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder and Sam Cooke, Beau will also be presenting a few songs in honour of Remembrance Day.

places.name: Indigenous Veterans Day Ceremony
places.address: Spirit Garden, Nathan Phillips Square, 100 Queen St W
places.description: Honour the bravery and sacrifice of those who served through the First and Second World Wars, the Korean War, Afghanistan, peacekeeping missions around the world and those who continue to serve in the Canadian Armed Forces. The ceremony includes traditional ways of honouring warriors from First Nations, Inuit, Métis, as well as non-status Indigenous veterans who served.

places.name: Daily Bread Food Bank: Volunteer
places.description: Sort donated food, pick orders for member food banks, or help prepare soups and casseroles for meal programs. Most shifts are at the warehouse in South Etobicoke.
highlights: Weekday shifts of about three hours
Register, then book a first volunteer session
Closer to home? Its Find a Food Bank page lists member agencies

places.name: Second Harvest: Volunteer
places.description: Canada's food rescue charity takes volunteers for administration, events, and group food sorts, based at its Toronto headquarters or online.
highlights: Group food sorts for 5 to 50 people
Summer lunch packing for kids' camps
Event support volunteers must be 19 or older
